item.title: Everyone at United admits Jason Wilcox’s one transfer decision was a huge misstep
item.description: Everyone at United admits Jason Wilcox’s one transfer decision was a huge misstep Manchester United will face Como in the Champions League in a match that could prove pivotal in dictating the direction of their European campaign this season. The Red Devils currently find themselves 18th in the table after securing a win over Sabah FK, followed by a defeat at the hands of Atletico Madrid. Manchester United failed to strengthen their defence After the 2-0 loss in the Spanish capital, Lisandro Martinez underlined frustrations behind the scenes by criticising United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox , for his work in the transfer market. INEOS headed into the summer fully aware that the ageing and injury-prone Luke Shaw was the only senior left-back at the club following the departure of Tyrell Malacia. Yet, Wilcox failed to bring in a left-back and, as everyone expected, with Shaw struggling with injury issues, Michael Carrick finds himself in a precarious position amid United’s disastrous run of form. Martinez has issued a formal apology for his outburst in Madrid, but it is difficult to disagree with the Argentina international, who remains a key part of the leaky defence, with just one clean sheet to show for this term. Man United hierarchy acknowledge they made a mistake According to The i Paper , Manchester United’s hierarchy are already looking at ways to overhaul the squad next summer. It is understood there is recognition, even among senior figures, that the defence should have been addressed in the summer. “Everyone at the club, at all levels, recognises United’s hierarchy made a huge misstep in not signing a left-back,” the report states. Lewis Hall was United’s preferred target for the left-back role, and it is claimed the Red Devils will revisit the deal for the Newcastle United man next summer. United are also long-term admirers of Bournemouth’s Adrien Truffert, but they are set to face plenty of competition for the French full-back’s signature. Furthermore, INEOS reportedly intend to sign at least one central defensive option and, should Martinez leave, they could sign another.

item.title: Man City boss Maresca backs hat-trick hero Foden to build on recent form – and gives update on Haaland
item.description: Man City boss Maresca backs hat-trick hero Foden to build on recent form – and gives update on Haaland Enzo Maresca has confirmed Erling Haaland will be fit to start against Aston Villa on Saturday following Manchester City’s 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens. The striker was rested against the Greek side, with Maresca pleased to have been able to manage the workload of several players. “He’s okay to start on Saturday,” Maresca said. “We had five or six players on the bench that were ready to come on but at the same time, they had a rest which is good. “I’m happy with that.” Phil Foden was the star of the night after scoring a hat-trick, with Maresca again backing the England international to rediscover his best form this season. “I was very happy with Phil, even before the red card,” he said. “I said since day one that I consider him one of the best English players. “For different reasons in the last two or three years, he was not good enough, but I know how good he is. “We are just trying to help him because we are sure that he’s going to help us this season.” Maresca added: “He’s a top player. “For different reasons, he had some problems in the last two years but I know he is going to help us. “That’s why I’m so keen to have him in the best way.”

item.title: Green, Robinson lead Pistons to season-opening win over Celtics
item.description: DETROIT — When the NBA released its 2026-27 schedule in August, promotional ads featuring the Detroit Pistons highlighted Cade Cunningham, Jalen Duren, and Ausar Thompson. This is fitting, as all three are considered core members of the franchise. However, coach J.B. Bickerstaff has consistently acknowledged that the Pistons' improvement over the past two years has come from factors beyond their core players' production. In the first game of the season, Bickerstaff’s belief was on full display as Javonte Green and Duncan Robinson delivered strong production, helping the Pistons overcome a 22-point deficit en route to a 121-113 comeback victory over the Boston Celtics Tuesday afternoon inside Little Caesars Arena. Green finished with 19 points, shooting 5-of-10 from the field and 5-of-8 from beyond the arc. Robinson added 21 points on 5-of-9 shooting from deep. Paul George led the Celtics with 38 points on 12-of-20 shooting, including seven made 3-point field goals. Derrick White added 17 points. Observations and notes ▶ Early 3-point shooting woes: It's only the first game of the season, and most shooters need time to find their rhythm in a new system, but the Pistons shot poorly from the arc. Before embarking on a 33-13 run midway through the third quarter, the Pistons began the night shooting 6-of-25 from behind the arc. Isaiah Joe shot 2-of-7 from deep. ▶ Thompson minutes: Bickerstaff stated during training camp that Ausar Thompson will play more minutes this season compared to last, when he averaged 26.0 minutes over 73 games. In the first game of the season, Thompson played 33 minutes. He added 11 points, 11 rebounds, and five assists. coty.davis@detroitnews.com @cotydavis_24 This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Green, Robinson lead Pistons to season-opening win over Celtics

item.title: Vasco announce squad for Copa Sul-Americana decider
item.description: Vasco announce squad for Copa Sul-Americana decider Vasco have officially announced their squad for tonight's clash against Boca Juniors. Kickoff is at 9:30 p.m. (Brasília time) at the Maracanã, with a place in the Copa Sudamericana semifinals at stake. Paulo Henrique will be available The main concern was the right-back's fitness. He came off against São Paulo with pain around his ribs. He did not complete Monday's training session but was included in the squad. Whether he starts will depend on fitness tests before kickoff. Pedro Emanuel will be without Andrés Gómez (suspended), Colidio (not registered), Spinelli and Barros (injured), and Matheus Carvalho (working his way back to full fitness). Vasco need only a draw to reach the final after winning 1–0 in Argentina. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

item.title: Pat Freiermuth & Tyler Higbee Headline Week 7 Fantasy Football Must-Start Tight Ends
item.description: Sep 27, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth (88) is introduced before a game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If your draft-day tight end is giving you weekly headaches, you're not alone. The gap between elite TE1s and the rest of the field is wider than ever, leaving fantasy managers constantly searching for a streaming savior. When a sleeper tight end end sees sustained target volume, high route rates, and high-value end-zone looks, he becomes more than a desperation play. Whether you need a bye-week fill-in or a high-upside alternative to an underperforming starter, here are the top tight ends positioned to outshine their Week 7 projections. Hunter Henry: New England Patriots @ Chicago Bears Henry's Red-Zone Role Could Deliver Another Fantasy Payday Oct 18, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots tight end Hunter Henry (85) reacts after his touchdown against the New York Jets in the second half at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Henry has established a stable floor in New England's passing offense, earning at least four targets in four of his last five games. He logged back-to-back weeks with touchdown receptions, solidifying his role as a preferred option in the scoring area. The Bears feature a competitive defense, but they have shown vulnerability when defending tight ends inside the 20-yard line. Running a route on over 73% of dropbacks with a steady 19% target share, Henry offers both a dependable target floor and legitimate touchdown equity . He deserves immediate consideration as a starter in Week 7. Tyler Higbee: Los Angeles Rams @ Las Vegas Raiders A Favorable Matchup Makes Higbee a Sneaky Streamer Oct 12, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams tight end Tyler Higbee (89) drops a pass in the end zone as Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson (22) defends during the third quarter at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Higbee continues to be a relaible safety valve, posting 24 receptions on 29 targets through six games with an efficient 82.8% catch rate. Las Vegas enters Week 7 allowing 14.7 half-PPR points per game to tight ends alongside six touchdowns surrendered to the position. While Higbee's weekly target depth isn't elite, his strong route participation and red-zone involvement against a leaking Raiders secondary creates immense upside. Pat Freiermuth: Pittsburgh Steelers vs. New Orleans Saints Freiermuth Could Capitalize on a Defense That Gives Up Points Oct 18, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth (88) looks on during the third quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Freiermut

Harold Fannin Jr.: Cleveland Browns @ Tennessee Titans Fannin Jr. Offers the Kind of Upside Fantasy Managers Need Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick (29) breaks up a pass intended for Cleveland Browns tight end Harold Fannin Jr. (44) during the first half at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Operating as an intriguing option outside the consensus elite ranks, Fannin Jr. has quietly expanded his route tree over the past three games. Tennessee's defense has struggled to contain athletic tight ends over the middle, surrendering above-average yards per route run to the position. For managers in need of ceiling rather than a safe floor, Fannin Jr.'s athletic profile and growing target share makes him a high-upside option who could outperform baseline Week 7 rankings. Darren Waller: Carolina Panthers @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers Waller's Target Share Keeps Him in the TE1 Conversation Oct 4, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller (88) with the ball in the second half at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Waller has quietly maintained a solid presence in Carolina's passing attack, averaging 4.3 targets and 3.3 receptions per game with a high catch rate over 80%. He remains a core fixture inside the 20 with four red-zone targets on the season. The Buccaneers' defense has been prone to allowing chunk plays over the middle to tight ends, giving Waller plenty of room to operate as a high-efficiency safety valve for Bryce Young. Final Verdict: Who Is Worth the Risk? When setting your Week 7 lineup, structure your decision around whether your roster needs a safe floor or maximum upside. Safe PPR Options: Henry & Higbee lead the group. Henry offers the most complete blend of target volume and red-zone usage, while Higbee benefits from a Raiders defense that struggles against tight ends. Touchdown-Dependent Starts: Freiermuth sits firmly in this tier. His matchup against the Saints provides immediate scoring upside if he is fully healthy. Deeper-League Option: Look to Fannin Jr. for yardage upside. item.title: Fantastic Foden Fires Man City To Win Over AEK Athen
item.description: Phil Foden hit a hat-trick to underline his long-awaited return to form as Manchester City crushed AEK Athens 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday. After a significant dip over the last two seasons, Foden provided hope of a renaissance for the England playmaker with a sublime display at the Etihad Stadium. The 26-year-old, who has admitted struggling with mental health issues, hadn’t scored for 10 months prior to his goal in Saturday’s win against Ipswich. Long heralded as one of England’s brightest talents, Foden was left out of his country’s World Cup squad earlier this year in a damning sign of his fall from grace. Having ended his run without a goal in the Champions League since November 2025, Foden now has to produce nights like this on a regular basis to complete his revival. Elliot Anderson put City ahead early in the first half with his first goal for the club since his close-season move from Nottingham Forest. Foden doubled City’s lead before the break and although Stavros Pilios pulled one back for the Greek side after the interval, the Premier League leaders finished with a flourish. Rayan Cherki bagged City’s third goal in typically flamboyant fashion and Foden struck twice more to complete his treble. It was City’s second win in the league phase after beating Porto in their opening game and losing to holders Paris Saint-Germain last week. City’s future remains in limbo as they wait the result of their appeal against an independent commission’s verdict that they were guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules. With reports emerging that City are set to be hit with a massive points deduction that will almost certainly condemn them to relegation, this season’s Champions League campaign could be the club’s last for some time. Enzo Maresca and his players have shown little sign of being affected by the scandal, while City’s fans defiantly show their backing for the Abu Dhabi-owned club. They have won 10 of their 11 games in all competitions this season and even the absence of Erling Haaland couldn’t derail them. Fantastic Foden Manchester City’s French midfielder #10 Rayan Cherki (R) celebrates scoring the team’s third goal with Manchester City’s English midfielder #47 Phil Foden during the UEFA Champions League football match between Manchester City and AEK Athens at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 20, 2026. (Photo by Oli SCARFF / AFP) City started with Haaland on the bench after the Norway striker limped down the tunnel at the final whistle with a foot injury following his double against Ipswich. Maresca made eight changes from the Ipswich game, with 17-year-old academy graduate Floyd Samba showing flashes of his talent on the flanks. City’s understudies took just 12 minutes to seize the lead. Enzo Fernadez’s free-kick cannoned down off the bar and Anderson reacted quicker than the flat-footed AEK defence as the midfielder slotted into the empty net from 10 yards. Foden doubled City’s lead at the climax of an eye-catching move in the 34th minute. Exchanging passes in a blur of movement and precision, Foden and Rico Lewis cut through AEK with ease before Foden fired high into the roof of the net from an acute angle. Perhaps overconfident after such a one-sided half, City lost their focus, allowing Pilios to reduce the deficit with their first shot on target in the 52nd minute. City quickly regained their two-goal lead in the 57th minute. Picked out by Foden on the edge of the area, Cherki unfurled a balletic turn that took him into space for a fine finish in keeping with his graceful first touch. In the 65th minute, Cherki’s long ball was knocked down by Lewis and Foden arrived to caress his shot into the top corner from 18 yards. Foden made a perfectly timed run to tap home Ryan McAidoo’s cross in the 76th minute, sealing his first hat-trick for over two years. AFP The post Fantastic Foden Fires Man City To Win Over AEK Athen appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 49ers owner Jed York makes first public appearance since arrest
item.description: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York arrives for the NFL owners meetings Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026, in New York. (Yuki Iwamura/AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura) Clearly, San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was ready for his NFL suspension to end and wasted no time before reemerging in the public eye. Nearly two months after York was arrested in a prostitution sting operation on Aug. 23 near his Ohio hometown, York made his first public appearance at the NFL owners meeting on Tuesday in New York. USA Today reporter Chris Bumbaca posted a video showing York walking through the lobby and heading to the first day of the NFL's two days of meetings in Manhattan. Jed York is back https://t.co/8na4pmJltx - Chris Bumbaca (@BOOMbaca) October 20, 2026 The appearance comes eight weeks and one day after York's arrest first became public knowledge, with York pleading no contest to two misdemeanor charges in court on Aug. 24. York was ordered to pay $1,150 in fines and sentenced to serve one day in jail for each charge, which were served concurrently. York skipped the last one-day owners meeting, which took place in Atlanta on Aug. 26 - just three days after his arrest. 49ers CEO Al Guido attended in York's place for the meeting, which was mainly held to approve the sale of the Seahawks to the Khosla family. York's eagerness to return to work and get out from under the cloud of his arrest and suspension is not exactly a shock. He willingly kept himself away from the team for the first three weeks of the NFL season, even though the league hadn't officially suspended him yet. The NFL then gave him credit for those missed games in announcing his suspension on Oct. 2 , shortening his punishment. (Left unexplained in all of this is an ESPN report that York still traveled all the way to Melbourne, Australia, ahead of the 49ers' Week 1 game in the city against the Rams, even though York did not attend the game.) According to San Francisco Standard columnist Tim Kawakami, York was expected to "immediately be back in charge--publicly and privately--as soon as his suspension ended." Kawakami also believes that York's attendance at Tuesday's meeting means he'll be in Atlanta on Sunday, when the Niners face the Falcons. York did not answer questions from media members on Tuesday prior to the meetings starting and has not talked to the media at all since his arrest, only offering a single public comment via a statement when the NFL announced his suspension. More 49ers - Ex-Cowboys QB Troy Aikman: 'I love everything about the 49ers organization' - Grant Cohn accuses 49ers reporter David Lombardi of 'hugging' players in locker room - With a monster day and a viral meme, Mike Evans just became a true 49ers star - How a Bay Area high school landed 2 ex-49ers stars as coaches Full 49ers coverage For all of our Bay Area sports coverage, sign up for The Catch newsletter here. This article originally published at 49ers owner Jed York makes first public appearance since arrest .

item.title: Arsenal's Arteta wary of "individual quality" Bayern still possess without Olise
item.description: Arsenal's Arteta wary of "individual quality" Bayern still possess without Olise Mikel Arteta is unsure as to whether Michael Olise missing tomorrow's game is a boost for Arsenal against Bayern Munich tomorrow . “I don't know. You want to face the best players in these kind of games, and he's out," Arteta said during his press conference on Tuesday. "But look at their squad and the possible starting 11 that they have, first of all, as a team, how incredibly well coached they are. "The mindset that they have, the conviction that they have in every action. And then individual quality moments that they can create. “You look at the goals and chances that they generate. So that's the opposition that you want to be facing and we will be facing tomorrow,” he said. Wishing his opposite number Vincent Kompany well as he battles a stomach bug, Arteta vowed his side will "go for it” in Munich. “I'm really looking forward to the game. This is the stage, the kind of team, the kind of coach, the kind of club, stadium that you want to be involved in. “We've prepared for the game with loads of enthusiasm. We'll try to come here and win the game tomorrow,” he concluded.

item.title: Gasperini: ‘Roma in good shape, but worry for Pellegrini injury’
item.description: Gasperini: ‘Roma in good shape, but worry for Pellegrini injury’ Gian Piero Gasperini was glad Roma got their first Champions League victory against Slovan Bratislava , but also ‘worried’ by a new injury to Lorenzo Pellegrini. The Giallorossi were frustrated after two Champions League games, as they held Fenerbahce to a 1-1 draw away, then were 3-1 up against Real Madrid until conceding three almost identical goals from corners in seven minutes for a 4-3 defeat. They knew tonight that Slovan Bratislava represented a must-win game and emerged with a comfortable 4-0 victory thanks to Mario Hermoso, Nahuel Molina, Niccolò Pisilli and the Donyell Malen penalty. Gasperini wants more from Roma ROME, ITALY – OCTOBER 17: Gian Piero Gasperini, Manager of AS Roma, looks on before the Serie A match between AS Roma and Genoa CFC at Stadio Olimpico on October 17, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) “Undoubtedly the team is in good shape, but it mustn’t rest on its laurels,” Gasperini told Sky Sport Italia. “It has to do the essentials consistently, and on nights like this, it ought to be a little more precise too.” Goal difference could be essential for qualification at the end of the league phase, so hosting a side that lost 6-1 to Paris Saint-Germain inevitably feels like an opportunity to bump that up. “It was important for us to have the right approach from the start, both because we needed three points, and also that there are no easy games in the Champions League. I liked the way we played, and rotating we had no excuses about fatigue.” ROME, ITALY – OCTOBER 20: Nahuel Molina of AS Roma celebrates scoring his team’s second goal with Niccolo Pisilli during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between AS Roma and SK Slovan Bratislava at Stadio Olimpico on October 20, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) Roma rotated the squad partly due to injuries, but also lost tonight’s captain Pellegrini to a muscular issue at the start of the second half. “I saw very important responses from the squad, because the fixture list is packed and I need everyone to be up to the task,” continued Gasperini. “This allows us to go forward with confidence and expand the list of potential starters in this team. My only worry is that now we’ve got Bryan Cristante back on the bench, we risk losing Pellegrini for a while.” ROME, ITALY – OCTOBER 20: Mario Hermoso of AS Roma celebrates scoring his team’s first goal with teammates during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between AS Roma and SK Slovan Bratislava at Stadio Olimpico on October 20, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) Roma are gaining confidence and have some huge Champions League tests coming up away to Manchester United and Paris Saint-Germain. “They are incredible tests and give us the opportunity to grow even more. This is the spirit with which we will approach those games.”

item.title: 2026 WTA Finals: A complete guide to the exclusive year-end tournament
item.description: The 2026 WTA Finals is happening for the first time ever at Indian Wells from November 8-15. This tournament is small but prestigious, open to the eight top performing singles players and doubles teams of the year. In terms of importance, only the four Grand Slams supersede it. Here is what you need to know about this year’s singles tournament. MORE: Who benefits from WTA Finals moving to Indian Wells The WTA Finals singles draw Nov 4, 2023; Cancun, Mexico; Coco Gauff (USA) waves as she leaves the court after her match against Jessica Pegula (USA) on day seven of the GNP Saguaros WTA Finals Cancun. Mandatory Credit: Susan Mullane-USA TODAY Sports Credit: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The WTA Finals singles draw has three former champions as well as three former Indian Wells champions. Elena Rybakina is 49-14 this season with three titles, two are Grand Slams (Australian Open and US Open). She is the only player in the draw who is a previous WTA Finals champion (2025) and an Indian Wells champion (2023). Rybakina is hoping to finish the year as the WTA World No. 1 ranked player for the first time in her career. She will need a solid performance to do so as Aryna Sabalenka is in striking distance. Aryna Sabalenka is 47-10 this season with three titles. She is less than 1,000 ranking points behind Rybakina, and an undefeated champion of this event (round robin and playoffs) can earn 1,500 points. Sabalenka likes playing at Indian Wells and is the reigning champion. Mirra Andreeva is 50-16, and the French Open champion. She has played doubles at the WTA Finals (with Diana Shnaider), but this is her first time in the singles draw. Andreeva won Indian Wells in 2025. Jessica Pegula has two WTA titles this year and a 50-13 record. She was the 2023 WTA Finalist when the event was in Cancun, losing to Iga Swiatek. Coco Gauff won one title in 2026 and is the 2024 WTA Finals champion. With Pegula, she also previously played doubles at the WTA Finals. Elina Svitolina won two titles this year on her way to a 46-14 record. She is the 2018 WTA Finals champion. Linda Noskova won two titles in 2026 including Wimbledon. She is 35-15 this season. Karolina Muchova or Marta Kostyuk will take the eighth position. Muchova is the points leader, but Kostyuk could overtake her with great runs in Ningbo and Tokyo. Whoever does not claim the eighth spot will be an alternate along with Iva Jovic. Alternates are on site and only play in the event if a player in the draw becomes injured or ill. Unlike a regular tournament with a bigger draw, the players face their high-ranked peers from start to finish in this event. Iga Swiatek is absent from this year’s event. It takes a lot of hard work (and wins) to get here so she will likely play, but the other storyline with her is her stance toward Russian and Belarusian players because of her Ukrainian heritage and the longstanding Russia-Ukraine war. WTA Finals iconic photo. pic.twitter.com/AM997y4xrW — José Morgado (@josemorgado) November 1, 2024 Only four of the eight players were in last year’s event (Rybakina, Sabalenka, Pegula, and Gauff) so there will be new faces in the iconic photo including Andreeva, Noskova, and Muchova or Kostyuk. In 2025, the US had four Americans in the top eight with Pegula, Gauff, Madison Keys, and Amanda Anisimova. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Eagles’ roster moves are good sign for Saquon Barkley’s Week 7 return
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles haven’t had the services of running back Saquon Barkley for the last two games as he deals with a hamstring injury, but there is some optimism that his absence might end this week. The Eagles made a few roster moves on Tuesday that included the team waiving running back Jaydon Blue from the 53-man roster. While Philly did add Elijah Mitchell to the practice squad, the team now has just two running backs on its active roster. The Athletic’s Zach Berman believes this is a potentially good sign that the Eagles anticipate Barkley’s return in Week 7. MORE: Shannon Sharpe pushes Eagles’ Saquon Barkley out of Tier 1 RBs “Based purely on numbers, I would interpret this as a positive development for Saquon Barkley’s status,” Berman wrote . “After these transactions, the Eagles have 2 RBs on the active roster (Saquon Barkley, Dameon Pierce) and 1 RB on the practice squad (Elijah Mitchell),” he went on to add. “They go with 3 for gameday. Unless they add someone else to the practice squad or active roster this week, it’s a good sign for Barkley. There is still a lot of time left in the week for the Eagles to add someone else, but for now Eagles fans and fantasy football owners alike should be cautiously optimistic that Barkley’s return will come this week. A much-needed lift Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) hands the ball off to running back Saquon Barkley (26) against the Los Angeles Rams during the first quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Eagles sure could use a boost offensively. Not only has Philly scored 20 points or less in each of its last three games, including just 31 points combined in the two contests without Barkley, they are also slated to be without quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season . Hurts was ruled out for Week 6 with a superficial blood clot in his calf after he was cleated in the area back in Week 4, but it has now been discovered that Hurts might be out for the rest of the season after blood clots were found in his lungs. MORE: Eagles’ gross Jalen Hurts blood clot negligence highlighted by NFL insider Tanner McKee got the start in Hurts’ place, but he’s an obvious downgrade from the Eagles’ starter and it’s going to be tough sledding for Philly’s offense from here on out. Knowing that, the Eagles are likely to lean on Barkley even more, both as a runner and pass-catcher, so he could have a ton on his plate the rest of the season. And, who knows, if things continue to go south for Philly the rest of this season like everyone expects them to, Barkley could get traded before the Nov. 10 deadline. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Green Bay Packers: Matt LaFleur on roughing calls and Jordan Love
item.description: Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Monday that Jordan Love is not getting roughing-the-passer calls and should push officials harder for them. Oct 19, 2025; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) with wide receiver Matthew Golden (0) against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The Packers were flagged for roughing the passer three times in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s 23-13 win over the Dallas Cowboys . Dallas was not flagged for it once. Love was sacked three times, and the official game book credits Dallas with eight quarterback hits. LaFleur said he wants the rule enforced the same way for both teams. “At the end of the day, you just want it to be called both ways,” LaFleur said. “So if they’re going to call it one way, it should be called for the other team as well. And I feel like there’s been a lot of times when Jordan’s taken some close to potential roughing calls. He’s not getting the calls.” “I don’t know. I think he needs to be more of an a-hole to the officials or lobby for some of those calls,” LaFleur continued. “You see some guys do it, and it works.” The Green Bay Packers were flagged for roughing three times in the fourth quarter The first call cost Green Bay an interception. Carrington Valentine picked off Dak Prescott at the Green Bay 34 with 7:44 left and returned it 21 yards, but Lukas Van Ness was flagged for roughing on the play. LaFleur did not think the Van Ness hit was a foul. “What’s the definition? You get like a step before you have to hit the quarterback,” LaFleur said. “And I didn’t think it was a forceful hit to the quarterback.” Later on the same drive, a roughing call on defensive lineman Karl Brooks wiped out an incompletion and moved Dallas from the Green Bay 27 to the 13. The Cowboys turned it over on downs at the 14 on that drive. The third came with 1:03 left, when Evan Williams was flagged on a 7-yard completion, moving the ball to the 6. Prescott threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Ryan Flournoy two plays later. The Brooks hit “did look like body weight,” LaFleur said, and the staff did not agree on another of the calls. “I know there was some discussion amongst that play with the staff in regards to whether or not it was roughing,” LaFleur said. “So I think some guys saw it one way, some guys saw it another way.” The Packers send plays to the league for review after every game. “It helps us educate our players, and at the end of the day, that’s our job,” LaFleur said. “We’ve got to educate them on what they can and cannot do and make sure that we try to coach them up, and they’ve got to control themselves in the moment.” After the game Sunday, LaFleur called the total “far too many” and said the penalties were costly . You get like a step before you have to hit the quarterback,” LaFleur said. “And I didn’t think it was a forceful hit to the quarterback.” Later on the same drive, a roughing call on defensive lineman Karl Brooks wiped out an incompletion and moved Dallas from the Green Bay 27 to the 13. Matt LaFleur says Jordan Love “balled out” against Dallas Love completed 23 of 41 passes for 276 yards, a touchdown and an interception and ran for a 1-yard score before halftime. LaFleur, who called Love “a G” after the game , went further Monday. “I thought he balled out, and specifically yesterday. I thought he balled out,” LaFleur said. “He played about as good as you could have played and taking hits in the process.” “For him to be able to stand in there, especially after some of the abuse he took early on in the season, I think it’s a testament to him and his ability and just how tough-minded of a guy he is,” LaFleur continued. “But he’s doing a great job getting the ball out of his hands. He’s trusting his guys to go make plays for him.” Standing in against pressure was a requirement when the Packers scouted quarterbacks, LaFleur said. “Usually the old chuck-and-duck isn’t too good for anybody,” LaFleur said. Love said Sunday the hits come with the job. “As part of playing the quarterback job, you know, you got to be able to stand in that pocket and take some hits and still deliver balls,” Love said. The Packers (4-2) play at the Detroit Lions on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 3:25 p.m. CT on FOX.

item.title: How Phil Foden proved his worth at Man City with Champions League hat-trick
item.description: Manchester City reignited their Champions League campaign in emphatic style with a dominant 5-1 victory over AEK Athens, spearheaded by a Phil Foden hat-trick. Elliot Anderson netted his first goal for the club and Rayan Cherki was also on the scoresheet during a largely one-sided encounter at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday. The Greek champions mounted a brief resurgence early in the second half to reduce the deficit to 2-1 through Stavros Pilios, though it remained a rare moment of quality from the visitors. Even with a heavily rotated side, as Enzo Maresca handed opportunities to fringe players, City proved superior in all departments. Leading scorer Erling Haaland was rested following an injury scare and remained on the bench throughout the match. Elliot Anderson scored his first Man City goal (Reuters) Youngster Floyd Samba lined up in place of the Norwegian striker, but the evening ultimately belonged to Foden. Following two indifferent seasons and a frustrating opening to the current campaign after his sending off in last month’s Manchester derby, the midfielder has returned in style over recent days. Having scored in Saturday’s win against Ipswich – his first strike since last December – his treble represented his first Champions League goals in nearly 12 months. Were it not for the serious off-field situation hanging over the club, City’s routine victory might simply have been described as business as usual. Kervin Arriaga blasted over from an early attack for the visitors, but City quickly established control and took the lead after 12 minutes through Anderson’s first goal for the club. Erling Haaland was given a complete rest after a recent injury scare (AP) The England midfielder pounced from close range after Enzo Fernandez had clipped the bar with a free-kick. Allan revelled in space down the left wing and, after one good run came to nothing, a second saw him cut inside to crack a fierce shot against the goal frame from a tight angle. City doubled their lead in the 34th minute with a fine goal from Foden, who broke down the right and exchanged passes with fellow academy graduate Rico Lewis before lifting the ball over goalkeeper Alberto Brignoli. City wanted more and Fernandez went close early in the second half when he tried to pick his spot from distance, only for his effort to be deflected wide. AEK stunned City by pulling one back after 52 minutes when substitute Zini tore down the left before feeding Pilios on his inside. Pilios cut into the area and drove a powerful low shot past Donnarumma and into the far corner. The vociferous visiting supporters cranked the volume up even more, but thoughts of an unlikely fightback were swiftly killed off as City claimed their third. The vociferous visiting supporters cranked the volume up even more, but thoughts of an unlikely fightback were swiftly killed off as City claimed their third. Manchester City’s Rayan Cherki got in on the act (Mike Egerton/PA) (PA Wire) Foden was again involved, cutting the ball back for Cherki, but the goal was all about the touch and composure of the Frenchman. Cherki shaped to shoot with his right foot but instead flicked the ball behind him and turned to finish in style with his left. The fourth came moments later as Cherki picked out Lewis with a sweeping ball from halfway, whose lay-off was calmly stroked into the roof of the net by Foden. He completed his hat-trick 14 minutes from time when he arrived in the box to tuck home from Ryan McAidoo’s pass.

item.title: Gasperini: “Morale is high, but I’m worried about injuries.”
item.description: Gasperini: “Morale is high, but I’m worried about injuries.” Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini spoke to Sky Sport after the Giallorossi’s 4-0 win over Slovan Bratislava. “The team is doing well, they’re in good spirits. But they shouldn’t get too complacent; they need to keep doing the essentials and play consistently. On nights like this, they could even afford to be a little more precise.” “These are extremely important answers, because this is the schedule and we need everyone, when called upon, to be up to Roma’s demands. These are crucial signals, because they allow us to move forward with confidence and expand the number of players who can be considered potential starters, practically to the entire squad.” “The only thing that worries me a little is that every time we play these types of matches, we risk losing some players. We’ve got Cristante back, but we’re losing Pellegrini. In some areas, we’re really a bit limited. That’s the only danger, because otherwise, these are highly anticipated, extraordinary matches that represent an incredible test for us.” “From these games, regardless of the result, you always gain some extra information and still have the opportunity to grow. The Champions League is extraordinary for precisely this reason, and we’ll approach both matches with this spirit. It was important for us to play a serious match right from the start, both because we need to get the three points and because there are no easy opponents in the Champions League. There aren’t any in the league, let alone in the Champions League.” “We undoubtedly did well given the way we approached the match. I must say that we’re also rotating several players from one match to the next, and this allows us to keep most of the team fresh, or at least not have too many excuses related to fatigue. I think that by playing matches at this level, you can also find a better rhythm and condition, even if it’s perhaps a bit of an exaggeration to say so now. I have some players who are really good at the moment, and as long as they’re in this condition, it’s right to let them play.”

item.title: 🎙️Flick's verdict: PSG showed they're still the best team
item.description: 🎙️Flick's verdict: PSG showed they're still the best team Following the painful 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League, Hansi Flick spoke at a press conference to assess his players' performance. The German coach was blunt about the team's shortcomings at decisive moments in the match. Self-criticism over defensive errors and the opposition's superiority Flick stressed that the number of lapses proved costly: "We made too many mistakes, and at this level that is unacceptable. For the third goal, we should have closed down the shooter and put pressure on that area. That's why they won." Despite highlighting spells of good tactical organization, he acknowledged the Parisian side's quality: "PSG showed that they are still better than us in quick transitions. We lost, but we will learn from it." Fitness concerns and worries over Dani Olmo The Barcelona coach also acknowledged that fitness affected the team's performance in the closing stages: "In the last 15 minutes, we weren't at 100 percent physically. It's not an excuse, but the circumstances weren't ideal for preparing for this match." He also raised concerns ahead of the upcoming fixtures when discussing the fitness of Dani Olmo, who finished the match in discomfort: "We'll have to see how he is. He took a heavy knock and felt some discomfort, so we'll have to wait to assess his condition." This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇪🇸 here.

item.title: Three-peat? PSG make Champions League statement despite injuries in Barcelona thriller
item.description: Paris St Germain stayed top of the Champions League league phase on goal difference after late goals from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz sealed a thrilling 4-2 win over Barcelona at Parc des Princes. The victory gave Luis Enrique's side three wins from three games in the competition. Vitinha found the net from just outside the area in the 81st minute, moments after Lamine Yamal had drawn Barcelona level with a wonderful solo goal. Ruiz then made sure of the result shortly before the final whistle. Barcelona's defensive frailty proved costly, with the number of mistakes made at the back ultimately hamstrunging Xavi Espart and Yamal's second-half goals. Until the late flurry of goals, Barcelona had keeper Joan Garcia to thank for keeping them in contention. He made two saves in the first five minutes alone. Lamine Yamal scored but still ended up on the losing side (AP) At the other end, a driving run swept Pedri into the PSG area, but Matvey Safonov palmed his shot to safety. Anthony Gordon then missed a great opportunity at the far post. Garcia brilliantly kept out an attempt by Ferran Torres after he was played in by Joao Neves. Somehow PSG were denied the opener as they swarmed around the box firing off shots, with Barcelona's keeper again coming to the rescue. Torres had stepped off the bench as a 20th-minute replacement for the injured Ousmane Dembele, while Khvicha Kvaratskhelia also went off with a physical issue. But it was Desire Doue who put the defending champions ahead as half-time approached. The goal began with an error as Barcelona continued their theme of giving the ball away easily. PSG pounced in a flash, setting up Doue, who tucked a fine shot into the bottom left corner. England winger Gordon was denied by Safonov in a one-on-one with the keeper that also saw him accidentally kick defender Willian Pacho in the head. Barcelona trailed at the interval for the first time this season. It was Garcia's skills that were keeping them in touch as he made another superb stop early in the second half. But in the 56th minute the Spanish giants were level. Ousmane Dembele went off injured (Reuters) Fermin Lopez played a one-two with Espart that released the right-back, and his run ended with a slick finish. PSG should have retaken the lead in the 72nd minute only for Torres to hit the right post from point-blank range. Their second did arrive moments later when Lucas Hernandez powered home a header from a corner. Barcelona hit back as Yamal glided past Warren Zaire-Emery before pulling the trigger for a wonderful solo goal, but the champions rose to the occasion magnificently.

item.title: Complete 2026-27 Philadelphia 76ers roster after their busy offseason
item.description: The Philadelphia 76ers are a team looking to make some noise in the 2026-27 season following a very busy offseason. Led by new President of Basketball Operations Mike Gansey and an overhauled front office, the Sixers made the most noise with the big additions of Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, and others. The plan for the Sixers is to finally get over the hump. This is a franchise that has not won a title since 1983 and hasn't been past Round 2 since 2001. As James said on media day, he did not leave his family in LA just to lose in the second round. There are high expectations in Philadelphia. With that being said, Brown and James were not the only big additions to the roster. item.title: Tesla and SpaceX are discussing a possible merger, Musk says
item.description: Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to discuss a possible merger, Elon Musk said during the latter's third quarter earnings call Tuesday. Musk, who serves as CEO of both companies, said the special committees have not reached agreement on the terms of any transaction - and that there's no guarantee that they will. That said, he called the possibility of a Tesla-SpaceX merger a "good idea." "I think it would be a good idea," Musk said. "But it's really up the special committees of both companies." Earlier this month, Barclays published a client note suggesting a potential Tesla-SpaceX combination could be announced ahead of Te … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Urban Meyer issues a warning to Texas coach Steve Sarkisian
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Texas Longhorns started the season 4-0 and climbed to No. 1 in the country, but back-to-back losses to Oklahoma and Florida have put head coach Steve Sarkisian squarely on the hot seat. Now, one of the most accomplished coaches in college football history thinks that Saturday’s game against No. 7 Ole Miss could define Sarkisian’s legacy. Speaking on his podcast this week, three-time national champion Urban Meyer called the matchup with the Rebels “the most important game of Steve Sarkisian’s coaching career,” warning that a loss would leave Sarkisian known as the coach who “couldn’t get it done at Texas.” Texas’ Rough Stretch Texas opened the season by beating Ohio State 24-23 and later knocked off Tennessee on the road, taking over the top spot in the rankings along the way. But the Longhorns lost 27-24 to Oklahoma in the Red River Rivalry, and then fell to Florida by the same score in Austin last weekend. Things have gotten so rough that Sarkisian didn’t rule out benching Arch Manning after the loss to the Gators. It’s the second straight year that Texas has stumbled after entering the season with high expectations. The Longhorns were the preseason No. 1 team in 2025, but they finished 10-3 and missed the College Football Playoff after making back-to-back semifinal appearances in Sarkisian’s previous two seasons. To make matters worse, Texas still has to face Ole Miss and Heisman Trophy contender Trinidad Chambliss, followed by Mississippi State, Missouri, LSU, Arkansas, and Texas A&M. ‘This One Is a Rubicon’ Meyer laid out the stakes for Sarkisian on The Triple Option , which he co-hosts with Mark Ingram and Rob Stone as he issued a clear warning to the Texas coach. “This is the most important game of Steve Sarkisian’s coaching career,” Meyer said on the podcast. “He’s had a hell of career, but this one is, this one is a Rubicon… If they lose this one, I mean you are in serious trouble. He won’t make the playoff.” Meyer didn’t initially think that Sarkisian’s job would be on the line, but he did think his reputation would be. “I don’t think it’s his job. I think it’s just your legacy, though. You’re the guy that couldn’t get it done at Texas. Because he’s been there, he’s been there,” Meyer said. But after some more discussion, Meyer came around to the idea that Sarkisian could be fired if Texas misses the playoff again. And he compared the situation to what would happen at Ohio State, where he won a national title in 2014. “Let’s do this. Let’s just [imagine]… if this happens at Ohio State: [You’re] gone. So maybe you’re right,” Meyer said. “Could you imagine losing like that, three games? Who’s it equal to at Texas? So if all the sudden you lose three at Ohio State, I would always say in my mind, if that ever happened… I didn’t think that way, but wow.” Clearly, Meyer isn’t the only one who thinks that there’s a lot riding on Saturday for Sarkisian. And a loss to Ole Miss would only make the noise in Aust

item.title: Why ‘You Can See Everything’ Could Win Best Picture at the Oscars
item.description: The word disruptor is a vividly descriptive one, and it’s almost always applied to an individual. But it doesn’t have to be. item.title: Real Madrid and Barcelona remain keen on Arsenal star
item.description: Real Madrid and Barcelona remain keen on Arsenal star Martin Zubimendi was expected to play an even bigger role at Arsenal this season after becoming an important member of the team last campaign. However, the midfielder has struggled to secure regular playing time since the new campaign began, raising questions about his future at the Emirates. The Spaniard has also been played out of position when given opportunities, making his situation different from what many expected. Mikel Arteta was keen on working with him, but Zubimendi could now consider his options if his role does not improve. Real Madrid and Barcelona monitor Zubimendi Zubimendi attracted interest from Real Madrid and Chelsea during the last transfer window, although neither club completed a move for him. Speculation about a possible return to Spain has continued , with fresh interest emerging from two of the country’s biggest clubs. According to Team Talk , Real Madrid are still monitoring the midfielder, while Barcelona have also entered the race to sign him. The Catalan club reportedly believe he could strengthen their squad and sees an opportunity to recruit him if Arsenal cannot offer him the regular football he wants. Barcelona could look to take advantage of Zubimendi’s current situation, particularly if his lack of minutes continues over the coming months. A move could potentially happen in January or at the end of the season, depending on how circumstances develop at Arsenal. Martin Zubimendi (Photo by Yong Teck Lim/Getty Images) Arsenal face a decision over his future Zubimendi’s situation presents an important question for Arsena l. The club brought him in with expectations that he would contribute significantly, but his limited involvement so far could encourage interest from teams prepared to offer him a more prominent role. Arteta will have to consider whether the midfielder can become a more regular part of his plans as the campaign progresses. Arsenal may prefer to keep him and give him more opportunities, rather than allow a player with his qualities to leave before he has fully settled into the team. However, if the situation remains unchanged, interest from Real Madrid and Barcelona could become increasingly difficult to ignore. Both clubs may view the midfielder as an opportunity to strengthen their squads, particularly if he becomes available. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Australian Grand Prix hit by shock withdrawal of multiple world champion
item.description: Pramac Yamaha have announced the shock news that Toprak Razgatlioglu will miss the remainder of the 2026 MotoGP season. The Turkish talent suffered a nasty highside crash at the Indonesian Grand Prix last time out and requires shoulder surgery that will see him miss the final five races of the campaign. Pramac also confirmed Razgatlioglu’s replacement in the form of test rider and 2022 Moto2 champion Augusto Fernandez. The incident occurred during FP2 in Mandalika when Razgatlioglu was thrown in the air and landed on his shoulder, before appearing to pop back in the dislocation. “Loading tweet...” World champion ruled out of Australian Grand Prix Two-time WorldSBK champion Razgatlioglu said in a statement: "I‘m extremely disappointed to miss the Australian Grand Prix . “Phillip Island is one of my favourite circuits and a place where I‘ve enjoyed some very special moments during my Superbike career. I was excited about the opportunity to race here on the MotoGP bike, which makes this situation even harder to accept. “After further medical assessments following the crash in Mandalika, it became clear that my shoulder injury is worse than we first believed. As a result, I will undergo surgery in the coming days to give myself the best chance of making a full recovery and returning at 100 per cent. “This wasn‘t an easy decision, but after consulting with the doctors and the people closest to me, we are convinced it is the right step for my future.” Razgatlioglu had made a decent start to life in MotoGP (Credit: Red Bull Content Pool) Razgatlioglu had made a decent start to life in MotoGP (Credit: Red Bull Content Pool) The 30-year-old then paid tribute to his teammate Jack Miller, who will be racing in his final Australian Grand Prix before leaving MotoGP. He added: “I would also like to wish Jack all the best for his home Grand Prix. “Racing in front of your home crowd is always special, and with this being the final MotoGP event at Phillip Island, I hope he can enjoy a fantastic weekend and achieve a great result. I‘ll be cheering for him and the entire team from afar.” Pramac Yamaha confirm replacement for remaining MotoGP races Pramac team director Gino Borsoi commented: "We are very sorry for Toprak, as we know how much he wanted to race at Phillip Island and continue his journey with the YZR-M1. “He has been working hard to adapt to MotoGP, and it is disappointing that this injury will prevent him from continuing that process over the coming races. “However, his health must come first, and we will support him throughout his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on the bike when he is ready.” He added: “At the same time, we welcome Augusto Fernandez, who will step in for Toprak at Phillip Island and until Toprak is ready to come back. As Yamaha‘s test rider, he knows the bike well, and we are pleased to have him joining the team for these events. “We will work together to make the most of this opportunity while wishing Toprak a successfu

As Yamaha‘s test rider, he knows the bike well, and we are pleased to have him joining the team for these events. “We will work together to make the most of this opportunity while wishing Toprak a successful operation and a smooth recovery.” Razgatlioglu's move to MotoGP Razgatlioglu switched to MotoGP for the 2026 season after huge success in Superbikes where he'd raced at Phillip Island. He won the last two world championships with BMW, and a third with Yamaha in 2021. The No.7 has earned plaudits for his transition to Grand Prix racing, recording 21 points, ten fewer than seasoned teammate Miller. Razgatlioglu is contracted with Yamaha for another year, and should have a big advantage for 2027 when the series switches to Pirelli tyres, which he raced on in WorldSBK. He will be partnered by Moto2 title contender Izan Guevara, with Miller heading to Superbikes.

item.title: PSG beat Barcelona 4-2 in Champions League thriller to underline European title credentials
item.description: PSG beat Barcelona 4-2 in Champions League thriller to underline European title credentials Paris Saint-Germain strengthened their position as Champions League favourites with an entertaining 4-2 victory over Barcelona at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday evening. The reigning European champions extended their unbeaten run in the competition to 13 matches, ending Barcelona’s perfect start to the 2026-27 season. Goals from Desire Doue, Lucas Hernandez, Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz secured another statement victory for Luis Enrique’s side, who maintained their position at the top of the league-phase standings. PSG began aggressively, pressing Barcelona into mistakes and creating several opportunities inside the opening five minutes. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia struck the post after Pedri surrendered possession, while Doue and Ousmane Dembele forced saves from Joan Garcia. Barcelona gradually recovered, with Raphinha testing Matvey Safonov following a promising attacking move. PSG suffered a setback when Dembele sustained an apparent hamstring injury and was replaced by Ferran Torres before half-time. However, the hosts continued creating opportunities, with Garcia producing several impressive saves to keep Barcelona level. Their resistance finally ended in the 38th minute when Doue capitalised on another turnover and drove a powerful low shot into the bottom corner. Fermin Lopez squandered an opportunity to equalise shortly afterwards, allowing PSG to preserve their advantage at the interval. Barcelona responded strongly after the restart and levelled through 19-year-old Xavi Espart, who marked his Champions League debut with an excellent near-post finish. Hansi Flick’s side subsequently gained control and threatened to complete the turnaround. Torres struck the woodwork from close range, but PSG immediately punished the visitors emphatically when Hernandez headed home from the resulting corner. Barcelona refused to surrender, with Lamine Yamal producing a brilliant individual effort to restore parity in the 78th minute. The teenager escaped Warren Zaire-Emery before squeezing his finish past Safonov from a difficult angle. However, PSG responded almost immediately through Vitinha, whose superb volley from outside the penalty area restored their lead. Ruiz then completed the scoring, converting Achraf Hakimi’s low delivery to secure an emphatic victory. The result leaves PSG with nine points from their opening three Champions League fixtures, while Barcelona remain on six. Luis Enrique’s team have now beaten Manchester City and Barcelona in successive European matches, reinforcing their credentials as serious contenders to retain the trophy. Barcelona, meanwhile, have conceded in 18 consecutive Champions League games, highlighting defensive vulnerabilities that continue to undermine their attacking quality. PSG will visit Villarreal on November 3, while Barcelona host Aston Villa as they attempt to recover from their first defeat of the campaign.

item.title: LeBron James shrugs off criticism as his luxury commute becomes an NBA talking point
item.description: Source: headlinephotos/Depositphotos Few athletes live under a brighter spotlight than LeBron James. Every move he makes becomes a talking point within minutes. His new chapter in Philadelphia has already given fans plenty to talk and argue about. One evening produced two very different conversations. One was about pure basketball joy, and the other was about logistics, money, and image. Together they show how a single big night can carry both celebration and criticism. A dunk that shook Philadelphia LeBron James took the Philadelphia floor on Friday, October 16, and performed his famous chalk toss before tipoff. A sellout crowd of 19,746 packed Xfinity Mobile Arena for the 76ers’ preseason finale against Boston. In the first quarter, Tyrese Maxey lobbed a half-court pass to James, who finished the play with a two-handed alley-oop dunk that sent the crowd into a frenzy. It offered Sixers fans an early look at the transition connection Philadelphia hopes to use this season. James finished with 8 points, 8 rebounds and 7 assists in 25 minutes. Boston won 125-120 in overtime at Xfinity Mobile Arena, ending Philadelphia’s preseason with a loss. The pass that set it up Tyrese Maxey started the play with a long pass in LeBron’s direction. James locked eyes on the ball right away. He snared it and finished at the rim with ease for all the home fans. Maxey is a close friend of James. LeBron has credited him with swaying the decision to sign in Philadelphia. The two now want to run the floor and score in transition as often as possible. After the game, James said the team is still finding its rhythm. He noted they are only a couple of weeks in together. He admitted some kinks remain, but said plenty exists to build on. Source: headlinephotos/Depositphotos Why LeBron chose the Sixers On July 24, James announced that he would join Philadelphia after his agent, Rich Paul, held conversations with 27 NBA teams during the free-agency process. James agreed to a reported two-year, $8 million deal. The Sixers have not won an NBA championship since 1983. Fanatics Fest ran from July 16-19 in New York, and James appeared at the event on July 16. Five days after the festival ended, he announced his decision to join Philadelphia. James already had a separate long-term business relationship with Fanatics through a trading-card partnership signed in 2024. Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro proclaimed July 24 as LeBron James Day following the announcement. The designation reflected the considerable attention James’ move generated across Philadelphia and Pennsylvania. Inside the helicopter commute plan James is splitting his time between the Philadelphia area and New York City. He has used a helicopter to travel between New York and the Sixers’ facilities near their Camden, New Jersey, practice site. Front Office Sports reported that a typical one-way helicopter trip takes about 30 minutes, compared with roughly 90 minutes to 2 hours by car. Other reporting has placed the heli

Inside the helicopter commute plan James is splitting his time between the Philadelphia area and New York City. He has used a helicopter to travel between New York and the Sixers’ facilities near their Camden, New Jersey, practice site. Front Office Sports reported that a typical one-way helicopter trip takes about 30 minutes, compared with roughly 90 minutes to 2 hours by car. Other reporting has placed the helicopter journey at approximately 30-45 minutes, depending on the trip. The arrangement significantly reduces James’ travel time between the two areas. During a demanding NBA season, avoiding lengthy road trips can free up additional time for basketball preparation, recovery, and personal commitments. Who pays for the rides? LeBron is not paying for the flights. His spokesperson told Front Office Sports that the Fanatics deal includes access to its corporate aviation. Reports say that similar trips run about $4,000 to $10,000 each way. The arrangement also serves Fanatics. A branded helicopter carrying a global star gets attention every time it lands. Sponsors like that kind of visibility, and fans notice it quickly on social media and in headlines. The perk also explains why the ride has become such a big topic. A famous player, a big sponsor, and a busy commute make an easy story. Fans naturally want to know exactly who pays. Little-known fact: During a July 2026 conversation at Fanatics Fest, James explained that his growing interest in golf also connects to his broader ambitions in business and philanthropy. How LeBron responded to the chatter After the Celtics game on Friday night, James addressed the helicopter talk for the first time. He also said he has done it before. He simply called it “Just another way of transportation. That’s all.” Those were his first public comments on the rides. He is dismissing the concerns and insists it is much ado about nothing. The story had been building for over a week. His short answer keeps the story simple. Stars often avoid long explanations when a topic feels overblown. Still, the helicopter will probably stay in the headlines every time it lifts off near Camden or Manhattan. Source: Image Press Agency/Depositphotos What the preseason debut revealed At 41, James is heading into a record 24th season and his first with Philadelphia. He spent the previous eight years with the Lakers. One lob and a dunk made the arena feel brand new. Philadelphia also added Jaylen Brown by trade. He joins Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey on a roster that now threatens the reigning champion New York Knicks in the East. That depth raises expectations across Philadelphia. One preseason game offers thin evidence. Still, James looked active as a finisher and a passer, a balance that has defined his career. It should keep Philadelphia fans very optimistic about the season ahead. What comes next for Philadelphia The real test begins when games count. Preseason highlights fade fast, and opponents will adjust. The Sixers must turn flashes of chemistry into steady wins across a long season of constant travel and heavy scrutiny. The helicopter story will follow him. Each ride will invite questions about cost, safety, and focus. Winning is usually the surest way to quiet outside noise. A strong start would make the commute seem minor. For fans, the picture is simple. A veteran legend, a speedy guard, and a hungry city make a fun mix. Whether the helicopter lands softly or loudly, the season has real buzz and big hopes. TL;DR LeBron’s two-handed dunk off a Maxey pass electrified a sellout crowd of 19,746. He calls his helicopter rides “just another way of transportation.” Fanatics covers the flights as part of his existing deal. The Sixers now face the real test of turning chemistry into wins. Rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard delivered a breakout performance, while Jaylen Warren continued to establish himself as the Steelers' lead running back. item.title: Cam Heyward Once Again Elected to Esteemed Post for Steelers
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers captain Cam Heyward with the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year patch on his jersey against the Houston Texans on Jan. 12, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Pittsburgh Steelers have elected Cam Heyward as their NFL Players Association player representative, per source. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith, guard Mason McCormick and defensive tackle Keeanu Benton join Heyward the alternates. Earlier this year, Heyward was re-elected to the NFLPA’s executive committee. He’s serving a one-year term as one of 10 vice presidents, the others being Oren Burks, Zaire Franklin, Harrison Phillips, Tanoh Kpassagnon, Ted Karras, Case Keenum, Jonathan Greenard, Brandon McManus and Thomas Morstead. Jalen Reeves-Maybin is the NFLPA’s president. Heyward was first elected to the executive committee on a two-year term in 2024 and has served as a spokesperson in the Steelers ’ locker room. On Tuesday, Heyward detailed the Steelers’ preparation for their upcoming matchup with the New Orleans Saints in Paris. “They tell us, ‘Don’t eat too late, try to get some rest and then try to stay up as much as you can once you get there,'” Heyward said on “The Rich Eisen Show.” “You don’t wanna have your TV on or your iPad on the plane too long. But it’s gonna be a rough one once we get there. … We’ve gotta create an edge here, so I’m gotta make sure to take care of my body.” Related Headlines Steelers Player’s Wife Questions Making Trip to Paris ‘I Was Devastated’: Mike Tomlin Reveals His Welcome to the NFL Moment Buccaneers Fan Offers Reward For Lost Hat Read more at Steelers Now

item.title: Packers Coach Gets Bluntly Honest Before Josh Jacobs’ Return
item.description: The Green Bay Packers are hoping to have star running back Josh Jacobs back on the field this week against the NFC North rival Detroit Lions. After being without him for the first six games of the season, Jacobs was finally removed from the Commissioner’s Exempt List. Jacobs’ return could not come at a better time. Through six weeks, the Packers’ running game has been the worst in the entire NFL. MarShawn Lloyd has been unable to live up to the hype once again. Kaleb Johnson has been unable to find consistency. Both Chris Brooks and Pierre Strong Jr. have been solid, but nothing spectacular. Despite the lack of a legitimate running game, Jordan Love has been magnificent. He has completed 59.7 percent of his pass attempts for 1,684 yards, 11 touchdowns, and four interceptions. Those numbers have kept the Green Bay offense dangerous. That being said, offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich spoke out with blunt honesty ahead of Jacobs’ anticipated return. Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs (8) celebrates scoring a touchdown with wide receiver Bo Melton (80) against the San Francisco 49ers during their football game Sunday, November 24, 2024, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. Packers Coach Gets Blunt About Josh Jacobs’ Return to the Field While the return of Jacobs should provide a spark for the Packers’ offense, he won’t be able to fix all of the problems single-handedly. Stenavich made that clear during his meeting with the press on Tuesday. “Josh [Jacobs] will definitely help, for sure,” Stenavich said . “He’s an excellent player, and he’ll provide some good spark for our offense. So, I’m excited about that. But we just all need to do a better job.” Last season, the 28-year-old running back played in 15 games for Green Bay. He carried the football 234 times for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns, averaging a solid four yards per attempt. Jacobs also caught 36 passes for 282 yards and another touchdown. Simply having a legitimate threat on the ground will help open up the passing game more for Love. Jacobs will also give head coach Matt LaFleur and the offense a much-needed running back who can pick up tough yards in short-yardage situations. Only time will tell what kind of impact Jacobs can have early on in his return to the field. But, the offensive reinforcements are coming in the middle of what has become a three-game winning streak for the Packers. The team is set to become even more dangerous moving forward. item.title: NFL stars receive studio applause with pitchside comments at Champions League game in Paris
item.description: Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images New Orleans Saints stars Alvin Kamara and Cameron Jordan brought some American football humour to Paris on Tuesday night as they made a surprise appearance during CBS Sports’ Champions League coverage. The NFL duo joined the broadcaster’s team ahead of Paris Saint-Germain’s clash with Barcelona and wasted little time getting involved in the conversation. Kamara immediately raised a smile with a cheeky comment about what the sport should actually be called. “Oh you called it soccer? I thought it was called football?!” he joked, prompting laughter and applause from the studio. While Americans typically refer to the game as soccer, football remains the preferred name across Europe, something Kamara was clearly happy to play along with. Jordan also appeared to be enjoying the occasion as the pair soaked up the atmosphere surrounding one of European football’s biggest competitions. Their appearance offered a welcome change of pace from the usual pre-match discussion, with the CBS team clearly appreciating the humour. The Saints vs the Pittsburgh Steelers will be the first-ever regular-season NFL game in France this weekend. item.title: Carrick wants more clean sheets to turn season around
item.description: Michael Carrick after Manchester United's 1-1 draw at Leeds [Getty Images] "You're dead right. I can't argue with that." Michael Carrick's response was to the point. The question that prompted it in his pre-match news conference at a rain-lashed Giuseppe Sinigaglia stadium in Como concerned his side's failure to keep clean sheets. It was put to Carrick that it would help if United could manage some shutouts, and he was asked if he had figured out the problem. United have kept the opposition out just once in 10 games this season, against Azerbaijan champions Sabah FK last month. "There's definitely parts of our game we have to improve to make things easier. I am fully aware of that," said Carrick, whose side take on Como in the Champions League on Wednesday. The problem goes further than this season though. They managed six clean sheets in Carrick's 17 matches in charge last term, including two in their final three games. Prior to that they had only managed two all season, part of an overall tally of nine in 63 games under his predecessor Ruben Amorim. It is an extreme comparison given solid defence was the bedrock of Arsenal's Premier League title triumph, but the Gunners, who face Bayern Munich in Germany on Wednesday, have recorded seven clean sheets in 11 matches this season. Fulham's Josh King celebrates Lisandro Martinez's own goal at Craven Cottage on 20 September [Getty Images] Continuity of selection would presumably help Carrick achieve defensive stability. It has proved virtually elusive so far. Only once has Carrick been able to name the same back four, when Diogo Dalot, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw started the victory against Ipswich at Old Trafford on 30 August and kept their places for the trip to Everton the following week. Carrick described his fitness update before the Como encounter as "a mixed bag". That was largely based on him saying Netherlands defender Matthijs de Ligt was "fit and ready" after 11 months on the sidelines with the back injury that required surgery in May. Yet De Ligt was on the bench at Leeds on Sunday when Martinez went off with the thigh injury that prevented him travelling to Italy, and instead Carrick turned to Noussair Mazraoui, usually a full-back, for the central slot. United's defensive resources are stretched thinner as Leny Yoro is ruled out through suspension. Shaw is still not fit and is expected to be out for "a little bit longer" than the 10 days Kobbie Mainoo is going to miss, which could mean the left-back won't return until after the November international break.
