item.content:encoded: Michael Carrick after Manchester United's 1-1 draw at Leeds [Getty Images] "You're dead right. I can't argue with that." Michael Carrick's response was to the point. The question that prompted it in his pre-match news conference at a rain-lashed Giuseppe Sinigaglia stadium in Como concerned his side's failure to keep clean sheets. It was put to Carrick that it would help if United could manage some shutouts, and he was asked if he had figured out the problem. United have kept the opposition out just once in 10 games this season, against Azerbaijan champions Sabah FK last month. "There's definitely parts of our game we have to improve to make things easier. I am fully aware of that," said Carrick, whose side take on Como in the Champions League on Wednesday. The problem goes further than this season though. They managed six clean sheets in Carrick's 17 matches in charge last term, including two in their final three games. Prior to that they had only managed two all season, part of an overall tally of nine in 63 games under his predecessor Ruben Amorim. It is an extreme comparison given solid defence was the bedrock of Arsenal's Premier League title triumph, but the Gunners, who face Bayern Munich in Germany on Wednesday, have recorded seven clean sheets in 11 matches this season. Fulham's Josh King celebrates Lisandro Martinez's own goal at Craven Cottage on 20 September [Getty Images] Continuity of selection would presumably help Carrick achieve defensive stability. It has proved virtually elusive so far. Only once has Carrick been able to name the same back four, when Diogo Dalot, Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw started the victory against Ipswich at Old Trafford on 30 August and kept their places for the trip to Everton the following week. Carrick described his fitness update before the Como encounter as "a mixed bag". That was largely based on him saying Netherlands defender Matthijs de Ligt was "fit and ready" after 11 months on the sidelines with the back injury that required surgery in May. Yet De Ligt was on the bench at Leeds on Sunday when Martinez went off with the thigh injury that prevented him travelling to Italy, and instead Carrick turned to Noussair Mazraoui, usually a full-back, for the central slot. United's defensive resources are stretched thinner as Leny Yoro is ruled out through suspension. Shaw is still not fit and is expected to be out for "a little bit longer" than the 10 days Kobbie Mainoo is going to miss, which could mean the left-back won't return until after the November international break. Will Amass be the sixth left-back this season? Diogo Dalot became the fifth different player to start for Manchester United at left-back this season at Leeds - and Harry Amass could become the sixth [Getty Images] To many observers, the Manchester United left-back situation was one that could have been anticipated and should have been addressed in the summer. The fact United spoke to Manchester City about Algeria international Rayan Ait-Nouri on deadline day suggests they did view it as a potential issue. After starting all 38 Premier League games last term and the first three this, Shaw has played only twice since, and the number of games missed could reach double figures before the 31-year-old returns. When Diogo Dalot lined up at left-back against Leeds, he became the fifth different player to start there for United in six games. Aside from Shaw, none of the quintet could be regarded as a natural left-back. However, after it was suggested Martinez's post-match outburst following the defeat by Atletico Madrid was partly down to 20-year-old Ayden Heaven playing at left-back, sources did point out the youngster played more often in that role than in the centre during his youth days at Arsenal. It was also suggested in the summer that United's coaching team did not believe 19-year-old Harry Amass, who was Shaw's stand-in during pre-season, was yet at the right level. Amass' single appearance so far this season, as a substitute for the final 18 minutes against Sabah, backs up that view, although Carrick has countered it. "He's right in contention," Carrick said. "At some point, young players need an opportunity. It's just finding the right time. "Sometimes it's because there's an unfortunate thing happened to somebody else. Sometimes it's just you're doing so well we have to give you a chance. "All the young players are in a similar boat. There's maybe four, five, or six of them trying to make that next step in terms of getting into the team and trying to start games, and Harry's definitely one of them." We made best of transfer window - Carrick Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada (right), next to sporting director Jason Wilcox (second right) [Getty Images] The failure to sign competition for Shaw is a stick that has been used to beat Carrick and sporting director Jason Wilcox. There is sympathy amid the agent fraternity for Wilcox, who was given a budget to work to that many in the game felt was inadequate to address United's needs. There is a theory that the £50m spent to acquire Andrey Santos from Chelsea should have been diverted elsewhere. With Santos sitting next to him as he spoke to the media on Tuesday, it was hardly a topic Carrick was going to engage with. "When we've got injuries at different stages, we can always look at what could have been done and where we could have improved," Carrick said. "I spoke to you about making the best of the transfer window in the situation we had. This man next to us [Santos] was a big part of that. I'm delighted to have him. "We had to make decisions in the summer. We did what we could do and made the best of it." Latest Manchester United news, analysis and fan views Ask about Man Utd - what do you want to know?

item.title: PSG late show downs Barca in Champions League, Liverpool fight back
item.description: Holders Paris Saint-Germain made it three wins from three in this season’s Champions League, beating Barcelona 4-2 thanks to late goals from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz on Tuesday, while Liverpool clinched a dramatic comeback victory over Villarreal. Phil Foden scored a hat-trick as Manchester City thrashed AEK Athens 5-1, while there were also much-needed wins for Roma and Napoli. PSG kept their place at the top of the early league-phase table, but could yet count the cost of injuries suffered by Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at the Parc des Princes. Barcelona twice levelled against the two-time defending champions, but were ultimately well beaten as they slipped to their first defeat of the season. Hansi Flick’s men had won their previous 11 games in all competitions this term. Kvaratskhelia hit the post, Dembele hobbled off and Ferran Torres was denied by Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia in a fast-paced opening. PSG took a deserved lead in the 38th minute as Desire Doue collected the ball outside the area and thumped a shot into the bottom corner. Garcia made another excellent save shortly after the break from Achraf Hakimi, before Xavi Espart burst through to level for Barca against the run of play. Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos both pulled up injured within seconds of each other and had to leave the field. The home team continued to press, though, and Lucas Hernandez restored their advantage 18 minutes from time with a brilliant header, shortly after former Barcelona forward Torres hit the post. Lamine Yamal powered past Warren Zaire-Emery to equalise again seven minutes later. But Vitinha hammered home from outside the box in the 81st minute and Ruiz’s tap-in gave Luis Enrique’s team a second straight 4-2 Champions League win after seeing off Man City by the same scoreline last week. – Liverpool fight back – Liverpool battled back from two goals down to also maintain their 100-percent record by edging out Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield. Liverpool fell behind in the fourth minute when Georges Mikautadze pounced on a terrible error from Virgil van Dijk, before Villarreal defender Sergi Cardona strolled through their defence to make it two. Alexis Mac Allister pulled one back for the hosts nine minutes before half-time by heading in Kostas Tsimikas’s corner. Andoni Iraola’s men were level in first-half added time through Ronald Araujo’s back-post header after Cardona inexplicably left Rio Ngumoha’s cross. Mac Allister completed the turnaround by firing in from Ngumoha’s square pass, and half-time substitute Florian Wirtz’s first goal of the season gave the Reds some breathing space. Tani Oluwaseyi set up a nervy finish for Iraola, but Liverpool held on. At the Etihad, Elliot Anderson put Manchester City in front with his first goal for the club, tapping in a 12th-minute opener after Enzo Fernandez’s free-kick bounced back off the crossbar. Phil Foden scored a hat-trick as Manchester City thrashed AEK Athens 5-1, while there were also much-needed wins for Roma and Napoli. PSG kept their place at the top of the early league-phase table, but could yet count the cost of injuries suffered by Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at the Parc des Princes. Barcelona twice levelled against the two-time defending champions, but were ultimately well beaten as they slipped to their first defeat of the season. Hansi Flick’s men had won their previous 11 games in all competitions this term. Kvaratskhelia hit the post, Dembele hobbled off and Ferran Torres was denied by Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia in a fast-paced opening. PSG took a deserved lead in the 38th minute as Desire Doue collected the ball outside the area and thumped a shot into the bottom corner. Garcia made another excellent save shortly after the break from Achraf Hakimi, before Xavi Espart burst through to level for Barca against the run of play. Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos both pulled up injured within seconds of each other and had to leave the field. The home team continued to press, though, and Lucas Hernandez restored their advantage 18 minutes from time with a brilliant header, shortly after former Barcelona forward Torres hit the post. Lamine Yamal powered past Warren Zaire-Emery to equalise again seven minutes later. But Vitinha hammered home from outside the box in the 81st minute and Ruiz’s tap-in gave Luis Enrique’s team a second straight 4-2 Champions League win after seeing off Man City by the same scoreline last week. – Liverpool fight back – Liverpool battled back from two goals down to also maintain their 100-percent record by edging out Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield. Liverpool fell behind in the fourth minute when Georges Mikautadze pounced on a terrible error from Virgil van Dijk, before Villarreal defender Sergi Cardona strolled through their defence to make it two. Alexis Mac Allister pulled one back for the hosts nine minutes before half-time by heading in Kostas Tsimikas’s corner. Andoni Iraola’s men were level in first-half added time through Ronald Araujo’s back-post header after Cardona inexplicably left Rio Ngumoha’s cross. Mac Allister completed the turnaround by firing in from Ngumoha’s square pass, and half-time substitute Florian Wirtz’s first goal of the season gave the Reds some breathing space. Tani Oluwaseyi set up a nervy finish for Iraola, but Liverpool held on. At the Etihad, Elliot Anderson put Manchester City in front with his first goal for the club, tapping in a 12th-minute opener after Enzo Fernandez’s free-kick bounced back off the crossbar. Phil Foden made it two goals in as many games after scoring against Ipswich at the weekend, but AEK halved the deficit early in the second half through Stavros Pilios. Rayan Cherki capped a fine individual performance by sweeping in City’s third in the 57th minute. Foden later fired in his second and third goals in a comprehensive victory, despite Erling Haaland being rested after picking up a knock at the weekend. – Respite for Serie A clubs – Roma eased to their first Champions League win since 2019 as the capital club brushed aside pointless Slovan Bratislava 4-0 at the Stadio Olimpico. All four Serie A clubs in the competition lost last week, but Napoli made it two wins from two on Tuesday for the Italian sides. Massimiliano Allegri’s men were twice pegged back by Bodo/Glimt but eventually got the better of the Norwegians in a 4-3 thriller, as Scott McTominay scored a brace. Atletico Madrid played out a 1-1 draw with Stuttgart in Germany, despite playing much of the second half with 10 men. Borussia Dortmund ended a run of four straight away defeats in the Champions League with a 2-1 win over Sabah in Baku. Fenerbahce suffered another setback after last week’s humiliating 6-0 loss at Aston Villa, blowing a two-goal lead to be held 2-2 at home by Slavia Prague. PSV Eindhoven clinched their first victory with a 1-0 success at Porto. The post PSG late show downs Barca in Champions League, Liverpool fight back appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ngumoha And Mac Allister Get 9 | Liverpool Players Rated In Hard-Fought Win Vs Villarreal
item.description: Ngumoha And Mac Allister Get 9 | Liverpool Players Rated In Hard-Fought Win Vs Villarreal Liverpool entertained Villarreal at Anfield earlier tonight as they hoped to secure a good result at home in the UEFA Champions League. The Reds made a slow start to the game and conceded the opener in the fourth minute when Georges Mikautadze found the back of the net. Sergi Cardona doubled Villarreal’s lead in the 29th minute before Alexis Mac Allister got a goal back for Andoni Iraola’s side in the 36th minute. Ronald Araujo equalised for the Reds in the first half injury time as the two teams went into the half-time break with a 2-2 scoreline. Mac Allister scored again for Liverpool in the 65th minute before Florian Wirtz got his name on the scoresheet just three minutes later. Tani Oluwaseyi got a goal back for Villarreal in the 87th minute, but the Merseyside outfit hung on and secured a hard-fought 4-3 win in front of their home fans. Let’s take a look at how each Liverpool player fared during the clash against Villarreal. GK: Alisson Becker – 6/10 He made a couple of good saves at the back, but would be disappointed after allowing three goals tonight. RB: Ronald Araujo – 7/10 Araujo didn’t do much wrong defensively and managed to score the equaliser in the latter stages of the first half. He got stuck in with some crunching tackles but failed to keep things solid at the back. CB: Virgil Van Dijk – 5.5/10 Van Dijk earned possession back twice but made a costly error at the back. LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 20: Rio Ngumoha of Liverpool runs with the ball away from Georges Mikautadze of Villarreal CF during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Liverpool FC and Villarreal CF at Anfield on October 20, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images) LB: Kostas Tsimikas – 8/10 He was caught out of position at times, but put in a lively performance inside the opponent’s half. Tsimikas has an assist to show for his efforts. CM: Ryan Gravenberch – 7/10 Gravenberch worked hard on both halves but lacked the cutting edge in the final third. CM: Trey Nyoni – 7/10 He anchored the midfield well and made two good chances going forward. RW: Rio Ngumoha – 9/10 Ngumoha made a lot of dangerous runs with the ball on the right flank and has a couple of assists to his name. CAM: Alexis Mac Allister – 9/10 He ran the show well inside the Villarreal half and managed to score a brace tonight. LW: Cody Gakpo – 8.5/10 Gakpo caused a lot of headaches for his marker and did well to secure an assist. ST: Lewis Koumas – 6.5/10 He worked hard but never looked like he would score. CAM: Florian Wirtz – 7.5/10 He combined well with his teammates and managed to score in the 68th minute with a composed finish. ST: Alexander Isak – 6/10 His impact on the game was minimal. CB: Joe Gomez – 6/10 Gomez failed to keep things solid at the back. He struggled to influence the game.

item.title: Foden thrilled after clinical AEK Athens display
item.description: Foden thrilled after clinical AEK Athens display Phil Foden expressed his elation after scoring a treble in our 5-1 UEFA Champions League victory over AEK Athens and expressed his hunger for even more goals. Match Report Foden treble inspires five-star City to AEK Athens triumph Elliot Anderson poked us ahead with his first goal for the Club before Foden rifled in a second shortly after the half-hour mark in our 150th fixture in the prestigious competition. Stavros Pilios pulled one back for AEK Athens seven minutes after the interval before Foden’s pass found Rayan Cherki to slot into the bottom corner and give us some breathing space. GALLERY: FANTASTIC FODEN HITS HAT-TRICK! Foden then took centre stage again, firing into the top corner for his brace, before completing his hat-trick from close-range, making it four goals and one assist in four days for the Englishman. “I enjoyed that a lot,” began Foden in an interview after the game. “The lads were great again. We showed determination again, it wasn’t pretty at times. We were giving sloppy passes away. “But, we stuck at the game plan and we kept going and in the end we broke them down. Overall I’m delighted. [My favourite goal is] probably the second to be honest. The way it went in. “I’m delighted to score goals now, I’m a forward so I have to keep scoring and helping the team. It’ll only do good for my confidence. “Slowly but surely [getting back to my best], still got a long way to go. I’m going in the right direction. Scoring along the way definitely helps. I’ve just got to keep working hard and try to be as best as I can for the manager and for the team. Especially when I changed into the false 9 role, I really enjoyed it a lot. In between the lines and in the pockets where I like to be and linking the play. I really enjoyed that role tonight.” The victory saw five debutants for City in the Champions League, with Floyd Samba, Allan, Ryan McAidoo, Vitor Reis and Kaden Braithwaite all getting their first taste of European football. Foden believes they all deserved their chance and confirmed he’s passing on all of his knowledge to the youngsters in the squad. “Just trying to help them as best as I can, along with the captains, like Ruben and Erling,” he continued. “Trying to help the young ones. “It shows the trust the manager has. We’ve got a lot of injuries at the moment and he’s not scared to use the young lads. “They’ve been playing really well so they deserved to play tonight. I’m really happy for them.”

item.title: Liverpool 4–3 Villarreal: Rio Ngumoha Earns 10/10 in Anfield Thriller
item.description: Liverpool 4–3 Villarreal: Rio Ngumoha Earns 10/10 in Anfield Thriller Liverpool 4–3 Villarreal – Champions League Man of the Match Rio Ngumoha Liverpool FC Rio Ngumoha delivered a sensational performance at Anfield, helping Liverpool recover from a dreadful opening half-hour to secure a dramatic 4–3 Champions League victory over Villarreal. The teenage winger was the catalyst for the comeback, bringing the crowd to its feet with a fearless display of direct running, creativity and attacking intent. The opening 30 minutes were horrid for Liverpool. Defensive mistakes and a lack of control allowed Villarreal to take advantage, leaving the Reds chasing the game on their own turf. While much of the team struggled to find its rhythm, Ngumoha was already showing the kind of confidence and determination that make him such an exciting prospect. Photo IMAGO Operating on the right wing, the England international has adapted remarkably well to a position that demands both technical quality and tactical discipline. He is not simply holding the width and waiting for the ball. He wants to take defenders on, attack space and make things happen. That willingness to be positive, even when the team is struggling, is a terrific quality to see in a young player. His contribution to Liverpool’s recovery was outstanding. Ngumoha supplied two assists, including the delivery for Alexis Mac Allister’s equaliser, and continued to trouble Villarreal with his movement and ability to beat opponents. His involvement in the attacking play gave Liverpool a much-needed spark and helped shift the momentum of a match that had threatened to get away from them. After the interval, he became even more influential. His wing play created the opportunity for Liverpool’s third goal, with his directness and close control leaving Villarreal struggling to contain him. Every time he received possession, there was a sense that something could happen. He played with the confidence of a player who believed he could change the outcome, and ultimately, he did. Ngumoha’s performance was not just about the assists. It was the energy, courage and willingness to take responsibility that stood out. At his age, there will inevitably be lessons to learn and consistency to develop, but displays like this demonstrate why the excitement around him continues to grow. He has the ability to become a major attacking weapon for Liverpool if his development continues on this trajectory. Alexis Mac Allister also deserves considerable credit after scoring twice and growing into the contest, while Jérémy Jacquet once again provided a reassuring presence in defence. However, Ngumoha was the standout performer by some distance. Liverpool needed inspiration after a disastrous start, and the teenager supplied it. His two assists and relentless attacking threat helped turn a difficult European night into a memorable Anfield victory. My pre-match prediction was Liverpool 3–1 Villarreal. item.title: (Video) Anfield DJ’s choice of music straight after full-time in Liverpool win was simply perfect
item.description: (Video) Anfield DJ’s choice of music straight after full-time in Liverpool win was simply perfect The full-time song choices at Anfield have been very much on point in recent games. At the end of Liverpool’s 0-3 defeat to Manchester City in thier first match back after the international break, during which the away side were found guilty of 114 charges of financial rule-breaking, the final whistle was followed by the strains of ‘Tell Me Lies’ by Fleetwood Mac ( talkSPORT ). Tonight the choice of post-match music swapped from being a not-so-subtle dig at the opposition to lauding the standout player from the Reds’ 4-3 win over Villarreal. Anfield DJ lauds Ngumoha with apt song choice Even though he didn’t get on the scoresheet on Tuesday, the undoubted star of the show was Rio Ngumoha, who tore the opposition apart with his electric dribbling and conjured a mesmerising assist to set up Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal of the night. BBC reporter Aadam Patel described the 18-year-old as ‘ a class apart ‘, and the Anfield DJ pointedly chose to play ‘Rio’ by Duran Duran straight after the final whistle. (Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Was this Ngumoha’s best Liverpool performance yet? Liverpool fans have been no strangers to Ngumoha’s precocious brilliance over the past year or so, but his performance tonight was arguably his best in a red shirt. As per Sofascore , he won eight of his 12 duels and completed seven out of eight dribbles whilst also executing three key passes, and Villarreal left-back Sergi Cardona will be quite glad he won’t have to come up against the Reds winger again any time soon. Liverpool Echo reporter Ian Doyle unsurprisingly gave him a 9/10 in his post-match player ratings as he wrote: ‘Dangerous runs offered encouragement opening quarter and persisted with great assist for the Liverpool second. Tormented Villarreal defence down right and brilliant work to set up third.’ Meanwhile, Daniel Sturridge – himself a superb attacker for the Reds in his playing days – gushed on Amazon Prime (via Sky Sports ) that Ngumoha has ‘God-given ability’ and a level of individual brilliance that ‘you can’t teach’. And to think he only turned 18 in August! Just think of how high a ceiling this kid could have… You can view the full-time footage from Anfield below, via @beth_lindop on X:

item.title: Jaxon Kohler receives injunction, will remain eligible for BYU
item.description: BYU’s Jaxon Kohler (0) shoots a layup during a game against Nebraska at the Marriott Center in Provo on Friday, Oct. 16, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News BYU’s last hurdle before the regular season has been cleared. Big man Jaxon Kohler will remain eligible for the Cougars, as a California court granted his preliminary injunction Tuesday for a fifth season of college eligibility. The news was first reported by Robby McCombs of Vanquish the Foe . According to CBS Sports college basketball insider Jon Rothstein, the NCAA will appeal the ruling. Sources: An injunction was granted in California for the Glancey V. NCAA case, giving all members of the Class of 2022 involved eligibility through the end of the 2026-27 college basketball season. The NCAA will appeal. — Jon Rothstein (@JonRothstein) October 20, 2026 As previously reported by the Deseret News , Kohler’s effort to receive further eligibility came in the aftermath of the NCAA’s new “five in five” eligibility model, which was not originally grandfathered to him as a class of 2022 high school graduate. Kohler, along with more than 70 other athletes, was granted a temporary restraining order against the NCAA in August as part of Glancey v. NCAA, allowing him to enter the transfer portal and land at BYU . The preliminary hearing for Glancey v. NCAA began in September and concluded Tuesday. The granted injunction means Kohler will remain eligible at least through the final trial date, which has yet to be determined. A four-year contributor at Michigan State who earned All-Big Ten honors last season, Kohler recorded a double-double of 10 points and 10 points in BYU’s preseason exhibition against Nebraska this past Friday, leading coach Kevin Young to call him “the perfect fit” at center for the Cougars. “It felt amazing, it felt surreal,” Kohler said after the Nebraska exhibition. “I mean, to play with these guys, to play for the community I was raised in and to go out there and be a Cougar, man, it was really special, to be honest.” This story will be updated. BYU’s Jaxon Kohler (0) shoots a 3-pointer during a game against Nebraska at the Marriott Center in Provo on Friday, Oct. 16, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News

item.title: Hermoso: “We’re a tough team, I like what I’m seeing.”
item.description: Hermoso: “We’re a tough team, I like what I’m seeing.” Following the 4-0 victory against Slovan Bratislava, Roma defender Mario Hermoso, who scored the temporary 1-0 lead, spoke to Sky Sport. “For us, it’s crucial to follow the coach’s instructions, do things well, and win. It’s also important to keep a clean sheet.” “Today was a really, really important match. We’d struggled after the defeat here against Real Madrid, and we absolutely needed to win this game, also for the standings.” “Certainly, it’s an important aspect, not just for us defenders, but for the entire team. We’re a tough team, who want to play with great intensity and always implement what the coach asks of us. That’s why keeping a clean sheet is crucial. We also have great talent up front, and we need to try to get as many balls as possible close to the opponent’s penalty area to allow our attackers to score.” “We have a strong team, a complete squad, and quality players in every position. We must continue to work and be the team we are. We all strive every day to give our all, and that says a lot about us, about the quality of the squad, and about the work the coach and the sporting director are doing. We must continue on this path, because it’s great to see Roma like this.”

We’re a tough team, who want to play with great intensity and always implement what the coach asks of us. That’s why keeping a clean sheet is crucial. We also have great talent up front, and we need to try to get as many balls as possible close to the opponent’s penalty area to allow our attackers to score.” “We have a strong team, a complete squad, and quality players in every position. We must continue to work and be the team we are. We all strive every day to give our all, and that says a lot about us, about the quality of the squad, and about the work the coach and the sporting director are doing. We must continue on this path, because it’s great to see Roma like this.”

item.title: NFL star challenges Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappé to a race courtesy of Thierry Henry
item.description: Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappé is one of the fastest players in soccer -Credit:Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto via Getty Images Widely regarded as one of the fastest players in the NFL, New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara has challenged Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappé - arguably one of soccer’s quickest players - to a race. This unexpected but potentially thrilling matchup arose on Tuesday courtesy of French soccer icon turned CBS Sports analyst Thierry Henry. Speaking from the CBS studio with Kamara and teammate Cam Jordan, who were pitchside in Paris ahead of PSG’s 4-2 UEFA Champions League win against Barcelona, the former Barça and Arsenal striker quizzed the duo on who was the fastest - with Kamara getting the nod. Cristiano Ronaldo delivers brutal Portugal 'ultimatum' after Jorge Jesus 'broke his word' Brentford report strange and 'dangerous behavior' during Liverpool match to police New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara is also known for his speed -Credit:Perry Knotts/Getty Images Henry then quizzed the Saints pair whether or not Kamara would be able to beat Mbappé in a race with a soccer ball at his feet, to which he replied, “Yeah…I’ve got it. Set it up. Look, I'm of African descent, so I think I've got a lot of football instinct in me.” This immediately prompted excitement from Micah Richards and Jamie Carragher in the studio, with Henry admitting he liked the 31-year-old’s “confidence.” Whether or not this race ever materializes, only time will tell. However, given that Kamara’s 40-yard dash time at the 2017 Combine clocked in at 4.56 seconds, and Mbappé reportedly got up to 23.4 mph at this summer’s FIFA World Cup, it could be a tight race. But if nothing else, this chat proved a moment to remember for Kamara as it gave him the opportunity to tell 49-year-old Henry, “Thierry, honestly, I have to say I’ve done a lot of damage with you on FIFA, so it’s good to talk to you.” It also provided Henry an excellent opportunity to subtly roast fellow analyst Richards, who asked the Saints stars what position he could have played if he’d given the NFL a try. “Waterboy,” Henry immediately replied. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE On a more serious note, Kamara suggested that the former Manchester City defender looked “like a good running back. Maybe a linebacker, a good athletic linebacker. But definitely a running back. You’re bigger than me.” Asked by Richards what assets he’d need to succeed, the five-time Pro Bowler explained, “You’ve got to have some speed. You've got to have some vision. And then it's the stuff you’ve got to have that is God-given. That nobody can coach…The stuff that makes the fancy plays.” Defensive end Jordan, 37, then chimed in, commenting, “After a guy like me hits you a couple of times, you’ll get used to avoiding me.” The Saints duo are in the French capital ahead of the NFL’s first-ever game in Paris, with New Orleans set to take on the Pittsburgh Steelers at the Stade de Fran

item.title: Tinubu mourns Afenifere leader Fasoranti
item.description: By Adeola Badru Afenifere has mourned its leader, Chief Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, recalling his contributions to Nigeria’s independence struggle, opposition to military rule and the campaign for the restoration of the annulled June 12, 1993 presidential election, as it described him as an exemplary leader whose life embodied patriotism, courage and service to humanity. The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation announced his passing in a statement issued on Tuesday by its National Publicity Secretary, Comrade Jare Ajayi, who said the centenarian, also known as Asiwaju Yoruba, died at about 4pm. Fasoranti, who turned 100 on May 11, 2026, was described by Afenifere as “a humanist, a philanthropist, an exemplary leader, a genuine patriot and a Yoruba leader and an icon” who remained a model of courage even in the most heart-rending circumstances. The organisation said the late elder statesman was the first of its leaders to attain the age of 100, having assumed the leadership of Afenifere in November 2008 following the death of his predecessor, Chief Abraham Adesanya, in August of the same year. According to the statement, Fasoranti followed in the footsteps of his predecessors by living an exemplary life from which individuals and organisations could draw inspiration and model their conduct. One of the frontline followers of the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo in the Action Group’s struggle for Nigeria’s independence, Fasoranti remained involved in progressive politics in the post-independence period. His lifetime spanned Nigeria’s colonial era, independence, the Civil War, successive military administrations and the return to democratic rule. Afenifere recalled that Fasoranti was actively involved in the National Democratic Coalition (NADECO), which spearheaded the struggle for the restoration of the June 12, 1993 presidential election won by the late Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola. The organisation said he participated actively in efforts to restore civilian rule whenever the military intervened in Nigeria’s political process, describing him as “a democrat par excellence”. It added that Fasoranti, like his political mentor, Awolowo, and his predecessors as Afenifere leader, the late Chief Adekunle Ajasin and Chief Abraham Adesanya, believed that public office should be used to serve the best interests of the people. Beyond his political engagements, the late elder statesman was an educationist who established Omolere Nursery and Primary School, Akure High School and St. Frances’ Academy in Igoba, Akure, Ondo State. He also served as Ondo State Commissioner for Finance between 1979 and 1983 under the administration of the late Governor Michael Adekunle Ajasin in the old Ondo State. Afenifere described Fasoranti as an unassuming progressive icon whose commitment to humanity, philanthropy and public service would continue to inspire individuals and organisations. Fasoranti, who turned 100 on May 11, 2026, was described by Afenifere as “a humanist, a philanthropist, an exemplary leader, a genuine patriot and a Yoruba leader and an icon” who remained a model of courage even in the most heart-rending circumstances. Afenifere recalled that Fasoranti was actively involved in the National Democratic Coalition (NADECO), which spearheaded the struggle for the restoration of the June 12, 1993 presidential election won by the late Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola. The organisation said he participated actively in efforts to restore civilian rule whenever the military intervened in Nigeria’s political process, describing him as “a democrat par excellence”. It added that Fasoranti, like his political mentor, Awolowo, and his predecessors as Afenifere leader, the late Chief Adekunle Ajasin and Chief Abraham Adesanya, believed that public office should be used to serve the best interests of the people. He also served as Ondo State Commissioner for Finance between 1979 and 1983 under the administration of the late Governor Michael Adekunle Ajasin in the old Ondo State. Afenifere described Fasoranti as an unassuming progressive icon whose commitment to humanity, philanthropy and public service would continue to inspire individuals and organisations. The organisation said it would “sorely miss this exemplary, unassuming, progressive icon who was a humanist and philanthropist in every sense of it”. It extended its condolences to the deceased’s immediate and extended families, the Ondo State Government and people, members of the Afenifere family in Nigeria and the diaspora, the Yoruba people worldwide and Nigerians, noting that Nigeria was a country dear to Fasoranti. item.title: PSG Overpower Barcelona For Third Champions League Win In A Row
item.description: Vitinha’s superb late strike proved crucial as reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain saw off rivals Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday in a dramatic game between two of the leading contenders to win this season’s Champions League. The match was poised at 2-2 when the Portuguese playmaker, who came third in last year’s Ballon d’Or ranking, controlled on his chest and fired in from just outside the box in the 81st minute at the Parc des Princes. Fabian Ruiz then sealed PSG’s third victory in as many matches in this season’s competition, as they aim to win the Champions League for the third season running. It had briefly looked as though Barcelona would leave the French capital with a point when Lamine Yamal, who is hoping to win this year’s Ballon d’Or, stabbed in Barcelona’s second equaliser on the night. Desire Doue had earlier opened the scoring for PSG, and Lucas Hernandez got their second goal after teenager Xavi Espart found the net for the Catalans. The defeat is a setback for Barcelona, albeit not one that is likely to seriously hurt their prospects of advancing further in Europe’s elite club competition. They had travelled to France on a run of 11 consecutive wins at the start of the season in all competitions. That sequence is now over, but the goals keep coming, and Yamal’s strike here was Barcelona’s 50th of the season all told. PSG, meanwhile, have now won seven games in a row between Ligue 1 and Champions League, but they lost both Ousmane Dembele — last year’s Ballon d’Or winner — and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to injury on the night. It remains to be seen how seriously hurt those two attackers are, although Doue was the real star of the show here and Luis Enrique’s team are well set to comfortably reach the knockout phase at this rate. This was the 14th meeting of the teams in the Champions League in the last 13 years, and for Barcelona it was probably not their biggest game of the week — beat Real Madrid at home this coming Sunday and they go nine points ahead of their great rivals in La Liga. Rodri on bench, Dembele injured Barcelona’s Spanish forward #10 Lamine Yamal (R) reacts at the end of the UEFA Champions League first round day 3 football match between Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and FC Barcelona at the Parc de Princes stadium in Paris on October 20, 2026. (Photo by JULIEN DE ROSA / AFP) That helps explain why Rodri, the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner, was left on the bench at kick-off, although Raphinha was back in the starting line-up after a recent spell out. Fresh from winning 4-2 at Manchester City last week, PSG almost scored inside 90 seconds as Kvaratskhelia hit the post, but they were dealt a blow as Dembele came off after just 20 minutes after pulling up with a hamstring injury. Ferran Torres replaced him, coming on to face the club he left in the summer, who themselves then lost Dani Olmo to injury as the action was interrupted. The match was poised at 2-2 when the Portuguese playmaker, who came third in last year’s Ballon d’Or ranking, controlled on his chest and fired in from just outside the box in the 81st minute at the Parc des Princes. Fabian Ruiz then sealed PSG’s third victory in as many matches in this season’s competition, as they aim to win the Champions League for the third season running. It had briefly looked as though Barcelona would leave the French capital with a point when Lamine Yamal, who is hoping to win this year’s Ballon d’Or, stabbed in Barcelona’s second equaliser on the night. Desire Doue had earlier opened the scoring for PSG, and Lucas Hernandez got their second goal after teenager Xavi Espart found the net for the Catalans. The defeat is a setback for Barcelona, albeit not one that is likely to seriously hurt their prospects of advancing further in Europe’s elite club competition. They had travelled to France on a run of 11 consecutive wins at the start of the season in all competitions. That sequence is now over, but the goals keep coming, and Yamal’s strike here was Barcelona’s 50th of the season all told. PSG, meanwhile, have now won seven games in a row between Ligue 1 and Champions League, but they lost both Ousmane Dembele — last year’s Ballon d’Or winner — and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to injury on the night. It remains to be seen how seriously hurt those two attackers are, although Doue was the real star of the show here and Luis Enrique’s team are well set to comfortably reach the knockout phase at this rate. This was the 14th meeting of the teams in the Champions League in the last 13 years, and for Barcelona it was probably not their biggest game of the week — beat Real Madrid at home this coming Sunday and they go nine points ahead of their great rivals in La Liga. Rodri on bench, Dembele injured Barcelona’s Spanish forward #10 Lamine Yamal (R) reacts at the end of the UEFA Champions League first round day 3 football match between Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and FC Barcelona at the Parc de Princes stadium in Paris on October 20, 2026. (Photo by JULIEN DE ROSA / AFP) That helps explain why Rodri, the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner, was left on the bench at kick-off, although Raphinha was back in the starting line-up after a recent spell out. Fresh from winning 4-2 at Manchester City last week, PSG almost scored inside 90 seconds as Kvaratskhelia hit the post, but they were dealt a blow as Dembele came off after just 20 minutes after pulling up with a hamstring injury. Ferran Torres replaced him, coming on to face the club he left in the summer, who themselves then lost Dani Olmo to injury as the action was interrupted. However, Paris opened the scoring in the 38th minute following an error by Yamal — he gave away possession in his own half, and the ball came to Doue who showed superb footwork before firing low into the bottom corner from just outside the area. The home side were worthy of their lead at the interval, yet Barcelona drew level soon after half-time as Fermin Lopez released Espart who drove into the box and fired in his second senior goal. Rodri soon entered the fray for Barca but the game became increasingly unbridled and Torres hit the post for the hosts just before Hernandez headed them back in front from a corner. The defender was called into the side to mark Yamal in the absence of usual starting left-back Nuno Mendes. The goal was just his third for PSG in over 100 appearances, and a first since February 2024. That crowned a fine performance for Hernandez, but he was substituted moments later by coach Luis Enrique, and replacement Warren Zaire-Emery was at fault for Barcelona’s second equaliser. He got caught underneath a high ball, allowing Yamal to run away and stab in his 10th goal of the campaign. PSG had the last laugh, though, as they reminded their opponents that they remain the team to beat in Europe this season with Vitinha making it 3-2 before Ruiz sealed the win from close range. item.title: Egypt involvement in Yemen 'may actually weaken Cairo's regional role', expert says
item.description: Egypt's parliament on Monday delayed a debate on President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi's request to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia until next week, state media reported, after an emergency session ended without a decision a day earlier. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Dr May Darwich, Associate Professor in International Relations of the Middle East at the University of Birmingham. She explains that "this kind of military operation does not really have any objectives or exit strategy so at the moment this might actually weaken Egypt's regional role".

item.title: FIFA U17 WWC: Flamingos beat Puerto Rico 2-0 to boost hopes
item.description: Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, boosted their chances at the ongoing FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco after securing a 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico in their Group B encounter in Rabat on Tuesday. The Flamingos, who won bronze at the 2022 edition of the competition, took the lead in the 25th minute through striker Oluwakemi Adegbuyi, who converted a pass from Queen Joseph. Nigeria started brightly, applying pressure on Puerto Rico’s defence and creating opportunities through quick passing and forward movement. Adegbuyi’s goal rewarded the team’s early efforts and gave Nigeria greater control of the game as the first half progressed. The Nigerian side continued to search for a second goal after the break, with Queen Joseph, Tosin Rafiu and Favour Nkwocha among those who threatened the Puerto Rican defence. Puerto Rico attempted to respond with tactical changes, but Nigeria coach Hakeem Busari also made substitutions to strengthen his team’s attacking options. Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku were introduced in the 67th minute as the Flamingos maintained their push for another goal. Their efforts paid off in the 90th minute when substitute Precious Oscar headed home a cross from Kemi Adegbuyi to double Nigeria’s lead and secure the victory. The Flamingos held on through six minutes of added time to claim all three points and strengthen their position in Group B. In the other group fixture, North Korea defeated Poland 6-1, setting up an important encounter with Nigeria on Friday. The result against Puerto Rico gives the Flamingos a boost ahead of the meeting with North Korea, which could prove crucial to their progress in the tournament. The post FIFA U17 WWC: Flamingos beat Puerto Rico 2-0 to boost hopes appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Carrick insists Manchester United board back him after Ten Hag points to ‘toxic culture’
item.description: Manager acknowledges he needs to start winning games Ten Hag accuses Cristiano Ronaldo of letting club down Michael Carrick believes Manchester United’s board continue to back him, although the manager admits he must start winning matches to keep his job. Carrick also denied there is a toxic culture at the club, after Erik ten Hag’s claim there had been when he was manager. Carrick’s side travel to Como on Wednesday for their third Champions League game, aiming for a third victory of the season in all competitions. Sunday’s 1-1 draw at Leeds left United 13th in the Premier League, having won only once. Continue reading...

item.title: Mac Allister double sparks Liverpool’s thrilling comeback win against Villarreal
item.description: Andoni Iraola and Iñigo Pérez parked their long and close friendship in the buildup to the Champions League duel between two old Athletic Bilbao teammates. They will have a humdinger of a contest to dissect when communications are restored. Liverpool, driven by Alexis Mac Allister and ignited by Rio Ngumoha, recovered from two goals down against Villarreal to maintain their 100% record in the competition in emphatic style. Mac Allister struck twice as Liverpool fought back from a tepid start to record a third successive win in all competitions. They were given a scare when Tani Oluwaseyi volleyed in a late third for Villarreal but were well deserving of their latest impressive result. Continue reading...

If successful, Musk said, the attempt would mark the first time in history an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered. "This is a profound technology milestone in the history of civilization consciousness," he said during the company's third quarter earnings report Tuesday . item.title: Foden hat-trick helps Manchester City cut through noise and crush AEK Athens
item.description: Enzo Maresca has called for Manchester City to make their own noise on the pitch to drown out the cacophony surrounding them but maybe a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium was what they needed all along. AEK Athens were easily dispatched in a businesslike manner, as Phil Foden announced his return to form with a hat-trick to get City’s Champions League campaign back on track after being pummelled by Paris Saint-Germain . The match was uneven throughout as Foden shone on the wing and later down the middle, with goals from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki helping to ease City to victory in front of half-full stands. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.title: Next-gen Xbox Could Cost Up to $1,800, New Report Says
item.description: It's no secret that the cost of video game hardware and computer components has been dramatically rising. We also know that the price of the next-generation Xbox console, codenamed Project Helix , is expected to be high. Microsoft has positioned Project Helix as a “ very premium, very high end ” device that's akin to a powerful gaming PC. But a new report puts the projected cost of the next Xbox console in stark relief: According to Microsoft's internal estimates, it could cost as much as $1,800.

item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 20, 1970: The Soviet Union launches last-ever Zond moon mission
item.description: null On Oct. 20, 1970, the Soviet Union launched the Zond 8 spacecraft on a mission to the moon. This was the last mission in the Zond program. After the first three Zond missions explored Venus and Mars , the next ones were circumlunar missions that flew around the moon before returning to Earth. Although there was no crew on board, the Zond spacecraft was designed with cosmonauts in mind. The Zond missions served as test flights for the Soviet Union's plans to send cosmonauts to the moon. But those plans for crewed flights never came to fruition. This was partly because the U.S. had already put astronauts on the moon , but also because the Zond missions had a lot of technical problems. Zond 8 was considered a success — even though its guidance system malfunctioned on the way back to Earth. The spacecraft still returned to Earth safely and splashed down in the Indian Ocean one week after it launched. The Soviet Union's Zond 8 spacecraft, the last in a series of lunar spacecraft, captured this image of Earthrise on Oct. 24, 1970. (Image credit: Moscow State University of Geodesy and Cartography) Why it mattered While the Zond 1 and Zond 2 missions were launched toward Venus and Mars, respectively, the primary target of most Zond missions was the moon. At the time, the Soviet Union was embroiled in an ongoing space race with the United States to be the first on the moon with a human crew. By the time Zond 8 launched on Oct. 20, 1970, that space race was lost to the Soviet Union. NASA and the U.S. had already landed astronauts on the moon twice with Apollo 11 and Apollo 12 (in July and November of 1969, respectively), and even peformed the first space rescue fo the Apollo 13 astronauts in April 1970. While Zond 8 was uncrewed, it was a test flight of the Soviet Union's L1 spacecraft that was designed to fly a cosmonaut around the moon. It looped around the moon in a lunar flyby, approaching within 1,120 kilometers of the moon's surface at its closest point, according to RussianSpaceWeb.com . An artist's illustration of a Zond spacecraft. (Image credit: Future) Cameras on Zond 8 captured stunning views of the Earth and moon, recreating the iconic Earthrise views seen by Apollo 8 astronauts two years earlier in 1968. Zond 8 ultimately splashed down in the Indian Ocean on Oct. 27, 1970 after a solar attitude sensor failed, sending it on a shorter, steeper reentry path during landing, according to RussianSpaceWeb.com. It was retrieved by a recovery ship, marking the end of the Soviet moon landing program. Russian would go on to develop a series of Salyut space stations , culminating in the long-lived Mir space station . After decades without a moon probe, Russia did launch a new uncrewed moon lander in 2023. That Luna 25 mission failed and crashed into the lunar surface after an onboard engine controller malfunctioned. The country has pledged a return to the moon in 2027. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive an

item.title: 2027: PDP, APGA, Accord join Tinubu’s re-election campaign — Yilwatda
item.description: -Says ruling party ready for Saturday’s campaign flag-off in Kaduna -As Yari promises issue-based campaign, says APC will showcase Tinubu’s achievements without insults By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, has claimed that major opposition parties, including the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and the Accord Party, have aligned with the ruling party’s campaign for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. Yilwatda stated this while speaking to State House correspondents shortly after meeting with President Tinubu alongside the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Senator Abdulaziz Yari, to brief him on preparations for the campaign. He said the development demonstrated the growing political support for the President, adding that the APC had completed preparations for the formal launch of its nationwide presidential campaign in Kaduna on Saturday, October 24. The APC Chairman said the party has attracted support from political parties that previously defeated the APC in elections, a development he described as evidence of the broadening political alignment around the President. According to him: “If you look at what the party is doing now, the oppositions are with us. All political parties that have defeated us in any election are all with us; PDP is with us, APGA is with us, Accord Party with us. These are the only political parties that have defeated us, except APM, and they are all with us in this campaign. “It shows that the entire Nigerian political cycle is Mr. President, and that’s what we’re doing now to ensure that we prepare for this grand flag off in Kaduna”, he declared. He, however, did not specify whether the claimed support represented formal endorsements by the national leaderships of the opposition parties or political alliances involving individual members and groups within them. Yilwatda expressed satisfaction with the level of preparations for the Kaduna campaign launch, saying the party’s leadership, campaign committees and state structures were fully mobilised for the exercise. He explained that his meeting with the President, alongside Yari, was intended to provide an update on arrangements for the event and the readiness of the campaign organisation to commence activities across the country. “We’ll flag-off the campaign on Saturday, 24th of October, and as you can see, we’re together with the DG to brief Mr. President on the preparation for the flag off. “For now, everything is set; the preparation is on, the members are motivated, the states, the committees are ready, and everything that is supposed to be done has been done”, he said. item.dc:creator: Akinbayo Wahab
item.content:encoded: -Says ruling party ready for Saturday’s campaign flag-off in Kaduna -As Yari promises issue-based campaign, says APC will showcase Tinubu’s achievements without insults By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, has claimed that major opposition parties, including the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and the Accord Party, have aligned with the ruling party’s campaign for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. Yilwatda stated this while speaking to State House correspondents shortly after meeting with President Tinubu alongside the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Senator Abdulaziz Yari, to brief him on preparations for the campaign. He said the development demonstrated the growing political support for the President, adding that the APC had completed preparations for the formal launch of its nationwide presidential campaign in Kaduna on Saturday, October 24. The APC Chairman said the party has attracted support from political parties that previously defeated the APC in elections, a development he described as evidence of the broadening political alignment around the President. According to him: “If you look at what the party is doing now, the oppositions are with us. All political parties that have defeated us in any election are all with us; PDP is with us, APGA is with us, Accord Party with us. These are the only political parties that have defeated us, except APM, and they are all with us in this campaign. “It shows that the entire Nigerian political cycle is Mr. President, and that’s what we’re doing now to ensure that we prepare for this grand flag off in Kaduna”, he declared. He, however, did not specify whether the claimed support represented formal endorsements by the national leaderships of the opposition parties or political alliances involving individual members and groups within them. Yilwatda expressed satisfaction with the level of preparations for the Kaduna campaign launch, saying the party’s leadership, campaign committees and state structures were fully mobilised for the exercise. He explained that his meeting with the President, alongside Yari, was intended to provide an update on arrangements for the event and the readiness of the campaign organisation to commence activities across the country. “We’ll flag-off the campaign on Saturday, 24th of October, and as you can see, we’re together with the DG to brief Mr. President on the preparation for the flag off. “For now, everything is set; the preparation is on, the members are motivated, the states, the committees are ready, and everything that is supposed to be done has been done”, he said. Speaking separately, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, said the ruling party would conduct a responsible and issue-based campaign anchored on the achievements of the Tinubu administration rather than personal attacks against opposition candidates. Yari, a former governor of Zamfara State, said the campaign council had resolved to focus on the record of the APC-led Federal Government and present its accomplishments to Nigerians as the basis for seeking another mandate in the 2027 presidential election. He maintained that the ruling party would avoid insults and name-calling, insisting that its campaign would be driven by evidence of government performance and the argument for continuity. “As a Council, what we say we are going to do? We are going to do a campaign with the records. A responsible campaign, no insults, no calling of names because there’s no name before us, but we have a record before us to show to Nigerians”, Yari stated. He explained that the campaign would provide an opportunity for the party to engage Nigerians on the policies and programmes implemented under the Tinubu administration and make the case for their continuation. “This is what our party did, this what our government did, so because of that, we are asking, pleading Nigerians to look at this record carefully so that they give us a second chance for continuity”, he added. The remarks came as the APC intensified preparations for its nationwide presidential campaign ahead of the 2027 general elections, with Kaduna designated as the venue for the formal flag-off. Yari had earlier announced, following a meeting with Tinubu on October 9, that the President had approved the campaign timetable, including planned visits to states across the federation. The Presidential Campaign Council was subsequently inaugurated on October 14, setting the stage for the commencement of the ruling party’s nationwide mobilisation activities. President Tinubu chairs the campaign council, with Vice President Kashim Shettima and Yilwatda serving as vice chairmen, while Yari oversees the day-to-day coordination of campaign activities as Director-General. The post 2027: PDP, APGA, Accord join Tinubu’s re-election campaign — Yilwatda appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘I’m alive’: Paris street medic isn’t dead, despite viral claims he was killed by police
item.description: A video showing French riot police violently beating a 26-year-old street medic in Paris has gone viral, with social media users falsely claiming he died from his injuries. But the street medic is alive, and spoke to FRANCE 24. The rumour was fuelled by confusion with a separate incident that same day: a man died of cardiac arrest in the same area, causing online users to conflate the two events. Vedika Bahl explains in Truth or Fake.

item.title: APC campaign: Tinubu has nothing to say to Nigerians — Baba-Ahmed
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has described President Bola Tinubu as a failure, alleging that the president has nothing to say to Nigerians as the 2027 general election approaches. Baba-Ahmed made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday, while criticising Tinubu’s administration over worsening insecurity, economic hardship and the impact of its policies on Nigerians. “Tinubu inherited Nigeria, but what has he done with it? He inherited a poor country; he inherited weak institutions; he inherited poverty and insecurity. We don’t blame him, but he’s been in power for three and a half years. He is a failure,” he said. The PRP chairman also questioned the president’s reported decision to campaign in only a few places, asking why Tinubu would not commit himself to meeting Nigerians and explaining his policies and the impact on their lives. “Why doesn’t Tinubu commit himself to say, I will. I have the energy, I have the intention, I want to see Nigerians, I want Nigerians to see me, I want them to hear me explain why they are more hungry,” Baba-Ahmed said. Asked why he believed Tinubu had indicated he would visit only a few places during the campaign, Baba-Ahmed replied: “Yes, he has nothing to say to them, I’m telling you, he has nothing to say to Nigerians.” He added: “The reason why he said, Go, gentlemen, go and campaign for me. I will stay here in Abuja and run the country. You’re running the country now? For three and a half years, you didn’t run the country, now you remember that you are here to run the country?” Baba-Ahmed also faulted the administration’s economic reforms, arguing that the difficult decisions taken by Tinubu had hurt ordinary Nigerians rather than improved their lives. “He (Tinubu) made some tough decisions but they were anti-people decisions, a tough decision doesn’t have to be a good decision,” he said. He questioned the impact of the administration’s policies on education, particularly for children living in areas affected by insecurity. “You talk about creating loans, that’s good, but do you know how many millions of children that can’t go to school under Tinubu’s watch in this country? Children who live in territories taken over by bandits, kidnappers, and who can’t go to school at all?” The PRP chairman further alleged that insecurity had deteriorated under the current administration. “Security has gotten considerably worse, it has never been worse like this,” he said. On the administration’s defence of its economic reforms, Baba-Ahmed dismissed the presentation of economic statistics as propaganda, arguing that the figures did not reflect the hardship experienced by ordinary Nigerians. “All these things you mentioned, this is the propaganda. Unfortunately, for Tinubu, Nigerians are not going to buy it. Children are not going to school, life is more insecure, life is harder,” he said. He argued that the president’s appeal for another four-year term would require Nigerians to accept that the current difficulties would eventually give way to better conditions. “He flashes all these statistics, he is saying, give me a second chance, even Tinubu will not say he made lives more better, what he will say is that yes, we are going through a difficult part, if you give me another four years, we will get better,” Baba-Ahmed said. He also questioned the administration’s economic sequencing, arguing that a government anticipating significant economic consequences from its policies should have considered their effects before implementing them. “You said the microeconomics is good, those are statistics that they use and they will tell you, if you give me another four years, I will see them. Sir, if you knew you had four years within which you’ll embark on a profoundly influential policy, shouldn’t you look at it first of all and say, I’m going to have four years and if I embark on these policies, it will have major economic impacts.” Baba-Ahmed added that a president should consider the immediate effects of economic policies on citizens before proceeding with them. “A thinking president will say let me do one or two things first, because I will impoverish people and the cost of transportation is vital and central to everything.” The post APC campaign: Tinubu has nothing to say to Nigerians — Baba-Ahmed appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UK reaffirms commitment to deepen defence, security partnership with Nigeria
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The United Kingdom has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening its longstanding defence and security partnership with Nigeria, with renewed focus on military cooperation, professional military education, institutional capacity building and enhanced operational effectiveness. Director of Defence Information, Major General Samaila Uba said the commitment was reiterated when the recently appointed British High Commissioner to Nigeria, Mr. Pete Vowles, paid a courtesy visit to the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General OO Oluyede, at the Defence Headquarters, Abuja. The British High Commissioner expressed appreciation for the enduring political, diplomatic and military relations between both countries, emphasising that defence and security cooperation remain critical pillars of the UK-Nigeria bilateral relationship. He underscored his determination to sustain the momentum of existing security initiatives and explore opportunities to deepen collaboration in response to evolving regional and global security challenges. He further highlighted the importance of maintaining a strong and mutually beneficial partnership that support regional stability and strengthens Nigeria’s capacity to address contemporary security threats. In his response, the CDS highlighted the longstanding historical ties between Nigeria and the United Kingdom, noting that both countries have sustained a productive defence relationship for several decades and continued to work together in addressing shared security concerns. General Oluyede emphasised the importance of sustaining and expanding existing areas of cooperation, particularly in professional military education, transfer of technology and institutional capacity building. He noted that ongoing defence agreements and training programmes have contributed to enhancing the professional competence and operational capabilities of the Armed Forces of Nigeria. The CDS stressed that continued collaboration with strategic international partners remains important to strengthening the Armed Forces’ capacity to respond effectively to emerging threats, while promoting greater self-reliance, institutional resilience and operational efficiency. Both parties expressed optimism about the future of the UK-Nigeria defence and security partnership, reaffirming their commitment to building on existing achievements and identifying further areas of cooperation for mutual benefit. item.title: Ogun Assembly backs establishment of state police
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State House of Assembly has thrown its weight behind the proposed establishment of state police, passing a resolution in support of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026. The resolution, titled “H.R. No. 194/OG/2025 – Consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (1999) (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 (Establishment of State Police Services),” was passed during plenary, following the consideration of a report by the House Ad-hoc Committee on Constitutional Review. The committee, chaired by a former Speaker of the Assembly, Rt. Hon. Olakunle Oluomo, presented its report on 26 clauses and proposed amendments to various sections of the 1999 Constitution. Presenting the report, Oluomo took the proposed amendments one after another, with lawmakers voting in favour of all the clauses and sections contained in the proposals. The amendments covered various aspects of the bill, including the substitution, insertion and alteration of specific constitutional provisions aimed at providing a legal framework for the establishment of state police services. Following the consideration of the proposed amendments, Oluomo moved a motion for the adoption of the committee’s report. The motion was seconded by Hon. Adegoke Adeyanju and subsequently supported by the lawmakers through a voice vote. The House Leader, Hon. Yusuf Sherif, thereafter moved a motion for the adoption of the report as a resolution of the Assembly. The motion was seconded by the Chief Whip, Hon. Omolola Bakare, and unanimously supported by members through a voice vote. Speaking after the passage of the resolution, the Speaker of the Assembly, Rt. Hon. Oludaisi Elemide, said the Assembly had joined other state legislatures across the country in supporting the establishment of state police, describing the decision as historic. Elemide said the resolution reflected the position of the lawmakers and the people of Ogun State on the need to strengthen the country’s security architecture through the establishment of state police services. According to him, the initiative would help improve security measures and enhance the protection of lives and property, while promoting the social well-being and economic development of the state. He added that the proposed establishment of state police was an important step towards addressing security challenges and strengthening the capacity to safeguard communities. Following the passage of the resolution, the Speaker directed that a clean copy of the document be prepared and transmitted to the National Assembly to formally communicate Ogun State’s support for the proposed constitutional amendment. The resolution forms part of the ongoing constitutional amendment process through which state legislatures are considering proposed changes to the 1999 Constitution, including the proposal to establish state police services. item.title: NASA to Conduct Low-Altitude Flights Over Texas Farmland
item.description: Editor’s Note: This article was originally published on Oct. 15, 2026, and has been updated to correct the location of the flights. A NASA Dynamic Aviation A200 aircraft will conduct low-flying research flights over farmland near Amarillo, Texas, from Thursday, Oct. 22, through Monday, Nov. 9. These flights will measure gaseous and particulate emissions from animal feeding operations. A photo of the Dynamic Aviation A200 aircraft, which will conduct low-flying research flights over farmland near Amarillo, Texas, to measure emissions in October and November 2026. Dynamic Aviation Agricultural emissions represent an important and understudied part of Earth’s land and atmosphere systems. The FarmFlux mission will deploy more than a dozen sensors to measure ozone, methane, ammonia, particulates, and other pollutants rising from crop lands and livestock farms and their interaction with the Earth’s atmosphere. The mission is jointly led by NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland; Colorado State University; and Boston University. Additional low-altitude research flights with a NASA P-3 Orion aircraft are scheduled for the March to July 2027 growing season in the Midwest and California’s Central Valley with a focus on cropland. For more information about the FarmFlux mission, visit: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/evs-4/farm-flux/ By Sharon Teitelbaum NASA’s Ames Research Center in California’s Silicon Valley

item.title: JustWatch, which tackles streaming fragmentation, launches own streaming service
item.description: Since launching in 2015, JustWatch has helped people navigate the growing number of streaming services by providing a guide on where to find movies they want to stream. Now JustWatch has its own streaming service and wants people to subscribe. Launched today, JustWatch TV offers some movies available for free with ads that aren’t free on any other streaming service, including Green Room (2015), Locke (2013), and Sing Sing (2023). Other free movies include Fiddlin ’ (2018 ), Friday the 13th (1980), and Hotel Mumbai (2018). I could play movies available for free on JustWatch TV without creating an account. JustWatch TV also has movies you can rent. Read full article Comments

item.title: Italy sends troops, toughens security laws after Milan clashes
item.description: Italy on Tuesday approved the deployment of 500 troops to Milan after violent clashes as fuel price protests hit pasta production and food deliveries in southern Italy. A cabinet meeting on Tuesday also approved a series of security measures, including making the detention of minors easier and introducing the crime of "violent participation in a demonstration". FRANCE 24's Seema Gupta reports from Rome.

item.title: Meta drops the word "train" from its commercial TOS after AI backlash
item.description: Hoping to quell criticism, Meta has dropped the word “train” from its “streamlined” commercial terms of service that kick in on October 30. Last week, Meta faced backlash after legal experts warned that the tech giant’s sweeping new commercial terms of service seemed to give Meta permission to endlessly scrape websites linked on business pages. Talking to Nieman Lab, experts suggested that Meta could possibly use the policy to avoid millions in licensing fees from news organizations by requiring all business users to share a wealth of AI training data simply for running a business page. A Meta spokesperson confirmed that Meta did not alert users to the changed language following backlash. This potentially only adds to confusion ahead of the policy rollout. In response to backlash, Meta's spokesperson provided a statement to Ars, acknowledging Nieman Lab's initial report but not its follow-up report reiterating experts' concerns: Read full article Comments

item.title: FG, Bi-Courtney end 20-year MMA2 dispute
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government and Bi-Courtney Aviation Services Limited have signed a final settlement to end a nearly 20-year dispute over MMA2, paving the way for renewed revenue generation and the completion of abandoned hotel and conference centre projects in Lagos. Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Tuesday in Abuja during the formal signing of the agreement, saying the settlement would enable the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) to begin receiving concession fees from MMA2 after years of litigation. Keyamo said the agreement followed the approval of the Federal Executive Council and the Federal Government’s decision under President Bola Tinubu to resolve the protracted dispute through negotiations rather than continued court battles. He described the settlement as a reciprocal arrangement under which both parties had agreed to relinquish outstanding claims to establish a framework for future cooperation. According to the minister, under the agreement, Bi-Courtney will waive its outstanding claims against the government, while the Federal Government and FAAN will release specified historical claims against the concessionaire, including accumulated concession fees and other related payments arising before the execution of the agreement. Keyamo said the arrangement would allow FAAN to commence earning revenue from MMA2, adding that the authority had not received concession fees from the terminal for about 20 years because of the dispute. He said the agreement also addressed a major point of contention concerning the General Aviation Terminal, known as MMA1, with the revised framework recognising the facility as belonging to the Federal Government and operated by FAAN. In return, the minister said the government had agreed to allow Bi-Courtney to expand its apron and accommodate regional flights within Africa at MMA2, subject to the terminal’s capacity. The settlement also covers separate lease arrangements for the four-star hotel and conference centre projects located opposite the airport terminal, whose unfinished structures have remained abandoned for years. Keyamo urged Bi-Courtney to fulfil its construction obligations and complete the projects, describing them as potential additions to the aviation and hospitality sectors. He said the government would work with FAAN and Bi-Courtney to ensure compliance with the agreement, particularly regarding construction, concession payments, airport operations and the agreed development programme. The minister added that regulatory oversight, airport security, emergency arrangements and maintenance standards would remain important under the revised contractual framework. Recounting the history of the dispute, Keyamo said the original concession agreement was signed on April 24, 2003, for the design, construction, operation and eventual transfer of the domestic terminal.
