According to the minister, under the agreement, Bi-Courtney will waive its outstanding claims against the government, while the Federal Government and FAAN will release specified historical claims against the concessionaire, including accumulated concession fees and other related payments arising before the execution of the agreement. Keyamo said the arrangement would allow FAAN to commence earning revenue from MMA2, adding that the authority had not received concession fees from the terminal for about 20 years because of the dispute. He said the agreement also addressed a major point of contention concerning the General Aviation Terminal, known as MMA1, with the revised framework recognising the facility as belonging to the Federal Government and operated by FAAN. In return, the minister said the government had agreed to allow Bi-Courtney to expand its apron and accommodate regional flights within Africa at MMA2, subject to the terminal’s capacity. The settlement also covers separate lease arrangements for the four-star hotel and conference centre projects located opposite the airport terminal, whose unfinished structures have remained abandoned for years. Keyamo urged Bi-Courtney to fulfil its construction obligations and complete the projects, describing them as potential additions to the aviation and hospitality sectors. He said the government would work with FAAN and Bi-Courtney to ensure compliance with the agreement, particularly regarding construction, concession payments, airport operations and the agreed development programme. The minister added that regulatory oversight, airport security, emergency arrangements and maintenance standards would remain important under the revised contractual framework. Recounting the history of the dispute, Keyamo said the original concession agreement was signed on April 24, 2003, for the design, construction, operation and eventual transfer of the domestic terminal. The concession, which commenced on May 7, 2007, was initially for 12 years but was subsequently extended to 36 years. Over time, disagreements over financial entitlements, concession obligations and ownership-related issues triggered multiple legal proceedings, some of which reached the Supreme Court. Keyamo said negotiations with Bi-Courtney’s chairman, Dr Wale Babalakin, and the respective legal and technical teams eventually produced an agreed settlement. He noted that the resolution had been achieved without the Federal Government engaging external lawyers for the negotiations. Speaking at the event, Babalakin thanked President Tinubu and Keyamo for resolving the dispute, which he said had remained unresolved for more than 18 years despite the parties having maintained their respective positions. He said the settlement would create employment opportunities, particularly through the completion of the abandoned projects, while improving the appearance of the airport environment. According to him, the agreement would also encourage investors who have encountered disputes with government to consider negotiated solutions as a viable means of resolving disagreements. Babalakin assured the government, the ministry and FAAN that Bi-Courtney would honour its commitments under the agreement. The post FG, Bi-Courtney end 20-year MMA2 dispute appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Arsenal’s David Raya hits back at ‘boring’ label as Arteta defends side’s style of play
item.description: Goalkeeper brushes off criticism before Bayern clash Kompany could miss game with virus affecting his legs David Raya says he does not care if rival supporters call Arsenal “boring” as his manager, Mikel Arteta, insisted that critics of the team’s style were only a “very small minority”. Arsenal made it 10 wins out of 11 in all competitions for the season when they beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 at the City Ground on Sunday. But it was a day when Noni Madueke’s late goal papered over a flat and one-paced performance. Arteta admitted his players had to be better in attacking terms and the discussion over how they are able to get the job done has tracked them to Germany where they face Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday night. Continue reading...

item.title: Gemini's Personal Intelligence is coming to cars
item.description: Google kicked off 2026 with the addition of Personal Intelligence to Gemini, allowing its AI to pull in more of your data to formulate answers. It started as a paid feature but eventually came to all Gemini users. However, this feature wasn't available in the car until now. Google is rolling out Personal Intelligence to Android Auto and Google Built-in, and it is still, thankfully, an optional feature. As Google points out , a generative AI's outputs are better "when it knows the world and knows you," which is correct in an uncomfortable sort of way. The more context you can provide to a model, the better the output will be at the end of the token shuffle. Since Google has so much of your data already, it sees Personal Intelligence as a differentiator versus other AI systems. You don't have to provide the AI context because it already has it from apps like Gmail and Calendar. Personal Intelligence is beginning its rollout in Android Auto today, and it will come to vehicles with Google built-in in the next few months. As an aside, "Google built-in" is questionable branding, but it refers to cars that run Google software in the infotainment system rather than projecting an interface from your phone. Very few vehicles have Google built-in, but Google often releases new car features on them first. This time, it's the other way around. Read full article Comments

item.title: Can’t make it to the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art for the 'Star Wars' display? This is the companion book set you’re looking for!
item.description: null Taschen, purveyors of fine art and design special-edition books, have teamed up with George Lucas and his newly opened Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles to present a masterful two-volume catalog of the museum’s illuminating offerings. Housed in a sturdy slipcase, readers will discover a pair of lavishly illustrated volumes spanning 832 pages and tipping the scales at nearly 14 pounds. At $200 for the pair, it's not cheap, but look on the bright side; hoisting these illustrated tomes will save you a subscription to your local gym! This immersive collection documents in great detail the astounding scope of rare items on display in Lucas’s treasury of paintings, murals, photographs, sculptures, posters, comic strips, illustrations, costumes, and magazine covers that have spurred humankind’s imagination. Developed in collaboration with George Lucas and the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, this extensive two-volume catalog brings together an unparalleled collection of narrative art. View Deal We'd absolutely recommend checking out the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in person if you can. Our own Chelsea Gohd visited the Los Angeles-based museum ahead of its opening in September 2026 and adored it. But if you're not a California local, getting lost in this collection's glossy pages is the next best thing to roaming the museum exhibitions on a rainy afternoon. Volumes I and II of Tashen's stunning "Lucas Museum of Narrative Art" edition (Image credit: Taschen) Far beyond a mere companion to the marvels inside the fantastic spaceship-shaped building poised near the University of Southern California campus — the same institution where Lucas attended film school in the late 1960s — these bold editions are an adventure in their own right. Waiting to be absorbed is an impressive assortment of storytelling expression that showcases beautiful works by everyone from Maxfield Parrish, N.C. Wyeth, and Norman Rockwell to Frank Frazetta, Jack Kirby, and Ralph McQuarrie. Lucas and his wife, Mellody Hobson, curated the museum’s contents that represent decades of collecting narrative art in all of its forms. From Taschen's "Lucas Museum of the Narrative Art" catalog (Image credit: Taschen) Our friends at Taschen were gracious enough to send us one of these Lucas Museum of Narrative Art special editions, and in unboxing this magnificent pair of books, one can feel the quality in the deluxe binding and thick covers. Inside you’ll find an eye-popping array of full-color photography and sharp descriptions for hundreds of artworks, all hand-picked by Lucas and Hobson. Lucas himself delivers the preface, which is titled "The Art of Story," where he professes his love of art, myth, anthropology, illustrators, and cinema. He recalls when he came to meet his mentor, Professor Joseph Campbell, and how he amassed 40,000 pieces of art beginning when he was a student at USC. Developed in collaboration with George Lucas and the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, this extensive two-volume catalog brings together an unparalleled collection of narrative art. View Deal We'd absolutely recommend checking out the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in person if you can. Waiting to be absorbed is an impressive assortment of storytelling expression that showcases beautiful works by everyone from Maxfield Parrish, N.C. Wyeth, and Norman Rockwell to Frank Frazetta, Jack Kirby, and Ralph McQuarrie. Lucas and his wife, Mellody Hobson, curated the museum’s contents that represent decades of collecting narrative art in all of its forms. From Taschen's "Lucas Museum of the Narrative Art" catalog (Image credit: Taschen) Our friends at Taschen were gracious enough to send us one of these Lucas Museum of Narrative Art special editions, and in unboxing this magnificent pair of books, one can feel the quality in the deluxe binding and thick covers. Inside you’ll find an eye-popping array of full-color photography and sharp descriptions for hundreds of artworks, all hand-picked by Lucas and Hobson. Lucas himself delivers the preface, which is titled "The Art of Story," where he professes his love of art, myth, anthropology, illustrators, and cinema. He recalls when he came to meet his mentor, Professor Joseph Campbell, and how he amassed 40,000 pieces of art beginning when he was a student at USC. From Taschen's "Lucas Museum of the Narrative Art" catalog (Image credit: Taschen) The great director Guillermo del Toro provides a heartfelt foreword praising the importance of the museum and these prestigious companion volumes depicting a multitude of visual wonders. Between the duo of volumes, sections are divided into chapters dealing with topics such as history, children's stories, the American West, everyday life, romance and adventure, photography, science fiction and fantasy, and, of course, Star Wars in Motion. From Taschen's "Lucas Museum of the Narrative Art" catalog (Image credit: Taschen) They take you on an overwhelming journey through the gallery’s incredibly diverse holdings, not least of which are archival items and concept art chronicling Lucas's involvement in the galaxy far, far away. This remarkable " Star Wars " section will be of particular interest to sci-fi aficionados, as it contains 100 pages of original props, paintings, concept artwork, costumes, models, and digital renderings created by some of Lucasfilm and Industrial Light and Magic’s best and brightest talents. From Taschen's "Lucas Museum of the Narrative Art" catalog (Image credit: Taschen) Taken with the rest of the 832 combined pages of Taschen's ambitious release that fully captures the dizzying breadth of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art , it's a brilliant keepsake to spark your soul and imagination. The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art two-book collection is available now via Taschen's website and Amazon . item.title: Logitech’s refurbished G Pro X2 Superstrike is 35 percent off
item.description: The Superstrike looks similar to Logitech’s previous high-end gaming mice, but it has haptics-based sensors instead of switches. | Image: Cameron Faulkner / The Verge Looking for a way to try the haptics-equipped G Pro X2 Superstrike wireless gaming mouse without spending full price? You probably aren’t alone. Logitech’s now-last-gen right-handed mouse is a great PC gaming companion that mimics the feel of mechanical switches with nothing but haptics. You can grab it refurbished through Logitech’s official eBay store for $131.74 (usually $179.99), and for even less with the code PROXPRODUCTS15 applied at checkout. It drops the price to just under $117. Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike Where to Buy: $179.99 $117 at eBay (refurb, w/ code PROXPRODUCTS15) The G Pro X2 Superstrike came out earlier this year, and I went hands-on with it. Logitech’s companion software lets you customize the intensity of the haptics, from an extra punchy click to one that’s barely there. (You can also turn the click feel off completely, but that felt a bit strange.) The mouse also supports rapid trigger, and when used together with haptics, it lowers the click latency compared with other mice that have mechanical switches. The company followed up recently with the X3 Superstrike , though its differences may not matter much to those who aren’t competitive gamers. The X3 features a more responsive sensor, better battery life, and improved weight distribution. There are some other somewhat small changes to the specs. That said, none of these improvements makes the X2 feel obsolete, and Logitech is continuing to support and sell the mouse. So, if you want to give it a try, now’s your chance to save quite a bit of money on the purchase. Read our hands-on of the X2 Superstrike.

item.title: Data depletion, poor network dominate NCC Consumer Parliament
item.description: By Efe Onodjae & Ogochukwu Agha Data depletion and poor network quality dominated discussions at the 95th edition of the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) Telecom Consumer Parliament, as telecommunications operators acknowledged the need to improve service delivery, transparency and communication with subscribers. The forum brought together representatives of mobile network operators, internet service providers, consumer advocacy groups, young people and the regulator to discuss ways of enhancing consumer experience and strengthening protection in Nigeria’s digital economy. The discussions centred on reliable connectivity, transparent billing, effective complaint resolution and ensuring that consumers receive timely information about service disruptions. Speaking during the panel session, Olubunmi Abejirinde, representing Airtel, said the company was investing in network expansion and capacity optimisation to improve service quality. She, however, acknowledged that more needed to be done to bridge the gap in communication between operators and subscribers, particularly during unplanned network disruptions. Abejirinde said while operators made efforts to inform customers about scheduled maintenance and planned network interruptions, communicating unexpected disruptions remained a challenge. She explained that customers relied on telecommunications services for essential activities, including financial transactions, communication with loved ones, education and other daily engagements, making timely information about service interruptions imperative. According to her, Airtel considers customer complaints an important tool for identifying service gaps, improving products and enabling management to make informed decisions on resolving recurring problems. She added that operators were aligning their activities with the NCC’s quality-of-service framework to improve compliance with service standards and strengthen complaint resolution. On data consumption concerns, Winifred Umerah, General Manager, Personal Strategy Management and Insights at MTN Nigeria, said the company had introduced measures to help subscribers better understand their network experience and monitor data usage. Umerah said MTN had invested more than $100 million in customer experience initiatives aimed at assessing subscribers’ actual experiences rather than relying solely on network coverage. She explained that the company’s Customer Experience Index was designed to help identify factors responsible for individual subscribers’ service challenges, including device limitations, network infrastructure and insufficient airtime or data balances. According to her, network coverage alone does not guarantee access to satisfactory telecommunications services, stressing the need for operators to assess the actual experience of customers. item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Okogba
item.content:encoded: By Efe Onodjae & Ogochukwu Agha Data depletion and poor network quality dominated discussions at the 95th edition of the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) Telecom Consumer Parliament, as telecommunications operators acknowledged the need to improve service delivery, transparency and communication with subscribers. The forum brought together representatives of mobile network operators, internet service providers, consumer advocacy groups, young people and the regulator to discuss ways of enhancing consumer experience and strengthening protection in Nigeria’s digital economy. The discussions centred on reliable connectivity, transparent billing, effective complaint resolution and ensuring that consumers receive timely information about service disruptions. Speaking during the panel session, Olubunmi Abejirinde, representing Airtel, said the company was investing in network expansion and capacity optimisation to improve service quality. She, however, acknowledged that more needed to be done to bridge the gap in communication between operators and subscribers, particularly during unplanned network disruptions. Abejirinde said while operators made efforts to inform customers about scheduled maintenance and planned network interruptions, communicating unexpected disruptions remained a challenge. She explained that customers relied on telecommunications services for essential activities, including financial transactions, communication with loved ones, education and other daily engagements, making timely information about service interruptions imperative. According to her, Airtel considers customer complaints an important tool for identifying service gaps, improving products and enabling management to make informed decisions on resolving recurring problems. She added that operators were aligning their activities with the NCC’s quality-of-service framework to improve compliance with service standards and strengthen complaint resolution. On data consumption concerns, Winifred Umerah, General Manager, Personal Strategy Management and Insights at MTN Nigeria, said the company had introduced measures to help subscribers better understand their network experience and monitor data usage. Umerah said MTN had invested more than $100 million in customer experience initiatives aimed at assessing subscribers’ actual experiences rather than relying solely on network coverage. She explained that the company’s Customer Experience Index was designed to help identify factors responsible for individual subscribers’ service challenges, including device limitations, network infrastructure and insufficient airtime or data balances. According to her, network coverage alone does not guarantee access to satisfactory telecommunications services, stressing the need for operators to assess the actual experience of customers. Addressing concerns over data depletion, Umerah said MTN had introduced a data-monitoring feature on its mobile application, allowing subscribers to review their consumption patterns and identify applications using the most data. She said the feature provides information on subscribers’ leading data-consuming applications over a seven-day period, adding that the company was working to improve consumer education on data usage. Umerah also encouraged subscribers to check the data-usage records available on their mobile phones and compare them with information provided by their service providers. She said such measures would help consumers better understand their usage patterns and hold operators accountable where discrepancies arise. The MTN representative acknowledged that the industry still had work to do to improve transparency and accessibility, noting that consumer trust should be an integral part of operators’ business strategies. Other panellists at the event included Kenechukwu Okonkwo of T2, Alamu Jewesimi of Globacom, Busola Akindele of Spectranet, Ayewoh Paul of Save the Consumer Initiative, Ojo Samuel, a cybersecurity and intelligence analyst representing young consumers, and Mistura Aruna of the NCC. The session highlighted the importance of collaboration among telecommunications operators, regulators and consumer advocacy groups in addressing persistent service challenges and improving customer satisfaction. The NCC Telecom Consumer Parliament provides a platform for stakeholders to discuss issues affecting telecommunications consumers and identify measures to improve service delivery, accountability and consumer protection in the country. item.title: Police rescue 11 Ghanaians lured to Nigeria with Canada visa offer
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State Police Command has rescued 11 Ghanaian nationals allegedly held against their will in Sagamu, Ogun State, after being lured to Nigeria with promises of Canadian and Spanish visas in a suspected international fraud scheme involving about ₦50.27 million. The victims, comprising seven males and four females, were rescued on October 19, following intelligence received by the police, according to a statement issued on Tuesday by the Command’s Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi. The statement said operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit swiftly mobilised to the suspected hideout after receiving actionable intelligence and successfully rescued all 11 victims. Preliminary investigations, according to the police, indicated that the victims were allegedly deceived by a fellow Ghanaian national who promised to facilitate their travel abroad. Each victim reportedly paid GH₵40,000 before being brought to Nigeria, where they were allegedly held against their will. However, the Command said investigations were ongoing to identify, track down and apprehend everyone connected with the alleged criminal network. The rescued Ghanaian nationals are receiving appropriate care and support, while detectives intensify efforts to unravel the circumstances surrounding their alleged ordeal. Reacting to the development, the Commissioner of Police in Ogun State, Bode Ojajuni, commended operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit for their prompt response and professionalism. Ojajuni reaffirmed the Command’s commitment to protecting lives, combating transnational crime and preventing criminal networks from exploiting unsuspecting members of the public. He declared that the state would not provide a safe haven for individuals who prey on the hopes and trust of others. “There is no safe haven for criminals who exploit the hopes of others,” the police commissioner said. He assured residents and members of the public that the Command would sustain its efforts to ensure that those responsible for the alleged crime were brought to justice. The Command urged members of the public to exercise caution when dealing with individuals or agents offering overseas travel and visa-processing services. It advised prospective travellers to verify the authenticity of travel arrangements and the credentials of service providers before making payments. The police also encouraged the public to report suspicious activities that could help security agencies identify and disrupt criminal operations. Reiterating its commitment to intelligence-led policing and effective collaboration with other security agencies, the Command said it would continue to take decisive action against criminal networks operating within the state. “Every credible lead matters, every life matters, and protecting the public remains paramount,” the statement added. The post Police rescue 11 Ghanaians lured to Nigeria with Canada visa offer appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: The Internet goes on high alert after discovery of 8 compromised TLS certs
item.description: Security personnel around the world are on high alert Tuesday following the discovery of eight TLS certificates with private keys so weak they could allow anyone to mint trusted browser and app credentials for any site on the Internet. As of late morning Tuesday, browser makers and some major apps and programming languages had blocked all eight of the intermediate certificates. There are no reports of certificate transparency logs, which track the issuance of all browser-trusted certificates, showing the compromised keys being used maliciously. The threat remains far from over, however, because it will be hard and time-consuming to update other key parts of the Internet, such as Linux distributions and embedded and Internet of Things devices. One word: bonkers The eight intermediate certificates belong to India-based certificate authority eMudhra Limited. An informal advisory published to emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com over on Tuesday posted the message “We have a problem here - Wayne.” The words were digitally signed using the private key of one of the eMudhra certificates. With proof that the reporting party had control of the key, defenders scrambled because the same key could be used to sign unauthorized certificates that would be trusted by millions of servers worldwide. Read full article Comments

As of late morning Tuesday, browser makers and some major apps and programming languages had blocked all eight of the intermediate certificates. There are no reports of certificate transparency logs, which track the issuance of all browser-trusted certificates, showing the compromised keys being used maliciously. The threat remains far from over, however, because it will be hard and time-consuming to update other key parts of the Internet, such as Linux distributions and embedded and Internet of Things devices. One word: bonkers The eight intermediate certificates belong to India-based certificate authority eMudhra Limited. An informal advisory published to emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com over on Tuesday posted the message “We have a problem here - Wayne.” The words were digitally signed using the private key of one of the eMudhra certificates. With proof that the reporting party had control of the key, defenders scrambled because the same key could be used to sign unauthorized certificates that would be trusted by millions of servers worldwide. item.title: APC opens door to Ikem as PDP crisis deepens in Cross River
item.description: …as PDP conclude plans to convene SEC over chairman”s exit By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, in Cross River State has thrown its doors open to Mr Vena Ikem, the former state chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, days after he quit the opposition party’s leadership citing a “crisis of direction.” APC state Chairman, Mr Chris Eta, said this in his Calabar office while responding to questions from journalists on whether the party was in talks with Ikem. “We’re not exactly in talks with Mr Ikem though but our party is bigger and still have enough space for anybody, including himself to come in,” Eta said. “We’ll welcome him if he decides that his party is not good enough for him like our great party.” Invoking the APC’s broom symbol, Eta said: “Our symbol is the broom. And you know when you sweep with the broom you could see sticks of the broom could be left on the floor. You’ll naturally want to pick them into the whole bunch.” Eta, however, declined to say whether Ikem had made any approach to the APC. Ikem, who piloted the PDP in the state for five years, resigned last week, saying he could no longer function effectively as chairman. In his resignation letter, he said he “found it increasingly difficult to reconcile his responsibilities as State Chairman with the prevailing internal dynamics and divergent positions that continue to weaken the party’s ability to pursue a clear and united course.” “The party is presently grappling with a crisis of direction and leadership coherence.” The tone of the letter suggested that Ikem had grown uncomfortable in the party he led, a development that has further fuelled speculation about his political future and the state of the PDP in Cross River. The APC chairman used the opportunity to extend a broader invitation, urging anyone interested and willing to join the ruling party to do so. Ikem’s exit is a fresh blow to the PDP, already weakened by internal wrangling, even as the APC continues to position itself as the party of choice in the state. Ikem has yet to publicly state his next move. However , the PDP in Swift response to his exit said the absence of one man does not have any effect on the party , as they remain formidable and would give the ruling APC a run for their money. Vanguard also learned that the Party would be convening its State Executive Committee (SEC) to deliberate on the way forward following the resignation of its former state chairman, Venatius Ikem Esq. In a statement released by the state Party Secretary, Mr Joe Bisong stated that the Party would convene its State Executive Committee (SEC) to deliberate on the way forward following the resignation of its former state chairman, Hon. Barr. Venatius Ikeem. In a statement dated October 17, 2026, and signed by the state secretary, Joe Obi Bisong, the party said it remained committed to strengthening its structures and pursuing its political ambition ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎Accordin

item.title: Nigeria Confirms Ebola Case in Abuja After Patient Arrives from Uganda
item.description: Following the Federal Government’s confirmation of an Ebola case in the FCT, health authorities have activated nationwide surveillance and urged the public to remain calm while strictly following official safety guidelines. The Federal Government of Nigeria has confirmed a case of the Ebola virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja . According to an official press statement issued on October 20, 2026, and signed by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate , the patient is a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda . She was admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received care for several days before laboratory confirmation established the diagnosis . She has since been moved to an isolation facility, where she is currently receiving medical care . In response to the development, the Federal Ministry of Health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), and the FCT Health Services Secretariat have mobilised a swift public health response to contain the spread . Contact tracing is already underway, with 44 close contacts—spanning healthcare workers, caregivers, patients, and travel companions—identified and placed under monitoring . Public health teams have also stepped up surveillance and are providing direct support to the hospital to reinforce infection prevention and control standards . Authorities have put all public and private healthcare facilities nationwide on high alert, urging medical personnel to maintain a high index of suspicion, isolate suspected cases promptly, and report them to health authorities immediately . Reassuring the public, the government noted that Nigeria successfully contained an Ebola outbreak back in 2014, building a robust public health framework and experienced response system . However, officials emphasised that safeguarding public health requires a collective effort . What Nigerians Should Know and Do Public health authorities have outlined essential guidelines to keep everyone safe while urging citizens to remain calm and avoid panic : How It Spreads: Ebola is transmitted through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected person who is exhibiting symptoms or has died from the disease, as well as through contact with contaminated materials . Individuals cannot transmit the virus before symptoms manifest . Stay Calm and Vigilant: Remain composed and rely strictly on verified updates from official health bodies to curb misinformation and stigma . Practice Good Hygiene: Maintain regular hand hygiene and strictly avoid contact with the body fluids of anyone suspected of carrying the virus . item.title: Cross River Assembly passes State Police Bill
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State House of Assembly, on Tuesday, threw its weight behind the creation of state police, passing the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, with all 22 members present voting in favour and none against, as lawmakers pushed for a decentralised policing system to tackle insecurity. Three of the Assembly’s 25 members were absent from plenary during the vote. The bill seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of State Police Services in the country. It contains 26 clauses and proposes 25 alterations through substitutions to provisions of the principal Act, including Sections 84(4), 89(2), 121(3), 124(4), 109(2), 153(1), 157(2), 158(1) and 160. Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Elvert Ayambem, said the vote reflected the Assembly’s commitment to supporting constitutional reforms aimed at addressing security challenges and protecting lives and property. “By this vote, the 10th Assembly has demonstrated its support for the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, which seeks to establish a constitutional framework for State Police Services,” he said. He stressed that implementation of state policing must be guided by the rule of law, accountability and democratic principles. Contributing to the debate, the Leader of the House and member representing Odukpani State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Francis Asuquo, argued that policing must be brought closer to the people. He said a decentralised system would sharpen security responses and address challenges peculiar to grassroots communities. The member representing Yala I State Constituency, Hon. Brian Odey, called for effective coordination between state and federal security agencies, to ensure the proposed State Police Services complement existing security structures and improve overall operations. The Deputy Leader of the House and member representing Abi State Constituency, Rt. Hon. Davies Eta, insisted on adequate safeguards, accountability and professionalism. He said state police must operate within the confines of the law and respect the fundamental rights of citizens. Lawmakers also cited improved intelligence gathering and better protection of lives and property as key benefits of a decentralised policing system. The passage marks the Assembly’s formal endorsement of the proposed amendments, paving the way for the establishment of State Police Services in Nigeria. The post Cross River Assembly passes State Police Bill appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: TP-Link tries to appease Trump admin with pledge to assemble routers in US
item.description: TP-Link yesterday announced plans to assemble Wi-Fi routers in the US, as the company attempts to get the Trump administration's approval to sell its newest routers to American consumers. The timing is uncertain, as TP-Link's press release said it expects US-based assembly to begin "as early as" 2027. TP-Link's application to sell new routers in the US could be rejected by the Trump administration or remain pending long enough to push the US-based assembly to 2028. "Pending US regulatory approval, TP-Link expects domestic assembly of its groundbreaking Wi-Fi 8 home networking product line to begin as early as next year," the company said. TP-Link said it signed a Letter of Intent with US company Keytronic, which agreed "to become a primary domestic manufacturing partner for TP-Link, supporting assembly of the company’s advanced networking portfolio in Corinth, Mississippi." item.title: 20 things you should know about Ebola
item.description: The Federal Government has reportedly commenced contact tracing after a suspected imported case of Ebola disease was identified in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), with 44 close contacts said to have been identified. Below are 20 things you should know about Ebola: Ebola is caused by a virus. It is caused by viruses belonging to the genus Orthoebolavirus. Ebola was first identified in 1976. The first recognized outbreaks occurred in what are now the Democratic Republic of the Congo and South Sudan. Ebola occurs primarily in sub-Saharan Africa. Most recognized outbreaks have occurred in African countries. Ebola can be deadly. Case-fatality rates have varied between outbreaks, sometimes reaching 80–90% or higher, depending on the outbreak and circumstances. Ebola does not spread simply by being near someone. Standing beside, walking past, or sharing public space with an infected person does not ordinarily transmit the disease. Ebola is not spread through the air like flu or COVID-19. Transmission primarily occurs through direct contact with infectious body fluids or contaminated materials. Ebola spreads through infected body fluids. These include blood, vomit, feces, urine, saliva, sweat, breast milk, semen, and vaginal fluids. People become contagious when symptoms begin. A person infected with Ebola is not considered contagious before developing symptoms. The incubation period can last 2–21 days. Symptoms most often begin around 8–10 days after exposure. Fever is a common early symptom. Other early symptoms include headache, muscle aches, weakness, and fatigue. Ebola can cause severe digestive symptoms. Vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain may occur as the illness progresses. Bleeding may occur in severe cases. Some patients develop unexplained bleeding, although bleeding does not occur in every case. Ebola can lead to organ failure. Severe illness can damage multiple organs and cause shock. Healthcare workers may face a high risk of infection. The risk increases when they care for infected patients without appropriate protective equipment and infection-control procedures. Family caregivers can also be exposed. Direct contact with an infected person’s body fluids without proper precautions can transmit the virus. Contaminated objects can spread Ebola. Needles, clothing, bedding, and medical equipment contaminated with infectious body fluids can transmit the virus. Safe burial practices are essential. The body of someone who has died from Ebola can remain infectious, making safe handling and burial procedures crucial. Animals can be a source of infection. Contact with infected wildlife, including certain bats and non-human primates, may expose people to Ebola viruses. Ebola is diagnosed through laboratory testing. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of blood is commonly used to detect the virus in living patients. Suspected cases require immediate medical assessment. item.title: Does anyone actually want to win the medium-lift race in the United States?
item.description: It has been 13 years since the debut of a new medium-lift rocket in the United States, the Antares vehicle developed by Orbital Sciences Corporation. The initial 100-series variant of the Antares rocket was kind of a hot mess. The rocket used old Soviet engines built during the era when Apollo astronauts were landing on the Moon. Decades later, in the 1990s, Aerojet acquired the engines and refurbished them for a rocket that would launch in the 2010s. Predictably, on the fifth launch of an Antares rocket in 2014, it exploded. The Antares vehicle is the last of a dying breed of medium-lift rockets—defined as having a lift capacity of 2 to 20 metric tons—in the United States. Nearly a decade and a half later there is a new generation of medium-lift vehicles coming online, and they are starkly different from Antares, which had not just Russian engines but a core stage manufactured in Ukraine. Read full article Comments

item.title: Ebola Virus: 7 things to know about causes, symptoms, prevention
item.description: Ebola virus is a dangerous virus that causes Ebola virus disease (EVD), a serious infectious illness that can be fatal. The virus can spread from infected animals to humans and from one infected person to another through direct contact with infected blood and other bodily fluids. Ebola can cause fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting and diarrhoea. In severe cases, the disease can damage vital organs and cause bleeding. However, not everyone who contracts Ebola dies. Early diagnosis and appropriate medical care can improve the chances of survival. Scientists believe that fruit bats may be natural hosts of the Ebola virus, although its natural reservoir has not been definitively confirmed. Humans may become infected through contact with infected wild animals, including fruit bats, monkeys, chimpanzees, gorillas and other susceptible animals. Causes and symptoms of ebola Ebola virus disease is caused by infection with an Ebola virus. The disease can affect several parts of the body and may become severe without appropriate medical care. Symptoms usually appear between two and 21 days after exposure to the virus, although they often begin within eight to 10 days. Early symptoms include sudden high fever, severe headache, extreme weakness, tiredness, muscle and joint pain, sore throat and loss of appetite. As the disease progresses, other symptoms may develop, including vomiting, diarrhoea, severe abdominal pain and skin rash. Some patients may experience unexplained bruising or bleeding from the gums, nose or other parts of the body. In severe cases, Ebola can cause complications affecting the liver, kidneys and other vital organs. However, not everyone with Ebola experiences bleeding. Fever, headache and weakness alone do not necessarily indicate Ebola because malaria, Lassa fever and other illnesses can cause similar symptoms. Medical assessment and appropriate laboratory testing are necessary to establish the cause of the illness. How ebola spreads Ebola spreads primarily through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person who has developed symptoms. These fluids include vomit, stool, urine and other secretions that may contain the virus. A person can become infected when these fluids enter the body through broken skin or the eyes, nose or mouth. item.dc:creator: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
item.content:encoded: Ebola virus is a dangerous virus that causes Ebola virus disease (EVD), a serious infectious illness that can be fatal. The virus can spread from infected animals to humans and from one infected person to another through direct contact with infected blood and other bodily fluids. Ebola can cause fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting and diarrhoea. In severe cases, the disease can damage vital organs and cause bleeding. However, not everyone who contracts Ebola dies. Early diagnosis and appropriate medical care can improve the chances of survival. Scientists believe that fruit bats may be natural hosts of the Ebola virus, although its natural reservoir has not been definitively confirmed. Humans may become infected through contact with infected wild animals, including fruit bats, monkeys, chimpanzees, gorillas and other susceptible animals. Causes and symptoms of ebola Ebola virus disease is caused by infection with an Ebola virus. The disease can affect several parts of the body and may become severe without appropriate medical care. Symptoms usually appear between two and 21 days after exposure to the virus, although they often begin within eight to 10 days. Early symptoms include sudden high fever, severe headache, extreme weakness, tiredness, muscle and joint pain, sore throat and loss of appetite. As the disease progresses, other symptoms may develop, including vomiting, diarrhoea, severe abdominal pain and skin rash. Some patients may experience unexplained bruising or bleeding from the gums, nose or other parts of the body. In severe cases, Ebola can cause complications affecting the liver, kidneys and other vital organs. However, not everyone with Ebola experiences bleeding. Fever, headache and weakness alone do not necessarily indicate Ebola because malaria, Lassa fever and other illnesses can cause similar symptoms. Medical assessment and appropriate laboratory testing are necessary to establish the cause of the illness. How ebola spreads Ebola spreads primarily through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person who has developed symptoms. These fluids include vomit, stool, urine and other secretions that may contain the virus. A person can become infected when these fluids enter the body through broken skin or the eyes, nose or mouth. Family members and healthcare workers may be exposed when caring for infected patients without appropriate protective equipment. The virus can also spread through contaminated objects, such as needles, clothing, bedding and medical equipment, particularly when they contain infectious bodily fluids. Another significant source of transmission is the body of a person who has died from Ebola. The body may remain infectious, making traditional burial practices involving direct contact with the deceased particularly dangerous. Humans may also contract Ebola through contact with infected wild animals, including certain bats and non-human primates. Ebola does not ordinarily spread through the air like measles or influenza. Simply walking past an infected person, living in the same city or travelling on the same flight does not automatically mean that someone will contract the disease. The risk depends on the nature of the exposure. Generally, people infected with Ebola are not considered contagious before symptoms develop. Nevertheless, anyone who has had contact with a confirmed case should follow public health instructions and seek guidance from health authorities. What to do If you suspect ebola infection Anyone who suspects they may have contracted Ebola should seek urgent medical guidance and follow the instructions of public health authorities. The first step is to contact the relevant health authorities if symptoms develop after contact with a suspected or confirmed Ebola patient or following possible exposure in an area experiencing an outbreak. It is important to call a hospital or healthcare facility before visiting. Informing medical personnel about the symptoms and possible exposure allows them to make appropriate arrangements to receive the patient safely and reduce the risk of further transmission. While awaiting medical guidance, the suspected patient should avoid close contact with other people and should not share items that may be contaminated with bodily fluids. People who suspect Ebola infection should not attempt to treat themselves with traditional remedies or take medicines without medical guidance. The disease requires specialised medical assessment and care. Treatment may include providing fluids to prevent dehydration, correcting electrolyte imbalances, managing complications and supporting affected organs. Specific antibody treatments are available for certain types of Ebola virus disease. Early diagnosis and appropriate medical care can significantly improve the chances of survival. Prevention of ebola Preventive measures are essential for reducing the risk of Ebola infection, particularly during an outbreak. People should wash their hands regularly with soap and water and avoid contact with the blood and bodily fluids of anyone suspected of having Ebola. They should also avoid touching the bodies of people who may have died from the disease. Handling sick or dead wild animals should be avoided, as some animals can carry the virus. Healthcare workers and caregivers should use appropriate protective equipment when attending to suspected or confirmed cases. Anyone who has been exposed to a confirmed Ebola case should contact health authorities promptly and follow their instructions on monitoring and other necessary precautions. Vaccines are available against certain types of Ebola virus, but they do not protect against every Ebola virus species. Vaccination programmes and other public health measures depend on the type of virus involved and the circumstances of an outbreak. Ebola Situation in Nigeria As of October 20, 2026, the Federal Government has announced a laboratory-confirmed case of Ebola virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). According to the government’s announcement, the patient was a woman who had recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda. Following the confirmation, the Federal Government called on public and private healthcare facilities nationwide to remain on high alert. Healthcare workers were urged to maintain a high index of suspicion, promptly identify and isolate suspected cases, observe strict infection prevention and control measures, and immediately report suspected cases to public health authorities. The confirmation of a case does not mean that everyone in Abuja or elsewhere in Nigeria is at risk of infection. Health authorities must assess the patient’s contacts and determine whether anyone had an exposure that could have transmitted the virus. People without a known exposure should remain calm, practise good hygiene and obtain information from official public health announcements rather than relying on rumours or unverified social media reports. Anyone who believes they may have been exposed to the confirmed case should contact the relevant health authorities for guidance. People who develop symptoms after a possible exposure should seek urgent medical advice and notify the healthcare facility before arriving. Difference between ebola and malaria Ebola and malaria can initially produce similar symptoms, particularly fever, headache and weakness. However, the two diseases have different causes and modes of transmission. Ebola is caused by a virus, while malaria is caused by parasites of the genus Plasmodium. Ebola is transmitted primarily through contact with infectious bodily fluids or contaminated materials, whereas malaria is usually transmitted through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito. item.title: DJI’s Osmo Pocket 3 vlogging camera is a good deal at under $400
item.description: DJI’s Osmo Pocket 3 is a big upgrade from your phone’s video quality.﻿ | Image: The Verge If you’re the kind of person who likes to document everything, either for professional and/or personal reasons, and your phone’s camera isn’t cutting it, you might be considering a dedicated vlogging camera. The DJI Osmo Pocket 3 is discounted to $395 (usually $499) at a variety of retailers, including Amazon , Best Buy , and B&H Photo . The large 1-inch sensor is mounted to a built-in gimbal that offers smooth, stable movement, letting you take impressive videos of your travels, activities, or daily routine. The built-in screen helps you frame shots and check footage on the go without pulling out your phone. DJI Osmo Pocket 3 The Pocket 3 features a 1-inch CMOS sensor, three built-in microphones, and a 2-inch rotatable screen. If you’re unhappy with the video your phone captures, DJI’s compact cam makes it easy to get high-quality, stabilized footage, whether you’re vlogging your adventures or filming a wedding. Read our impressions . Where to Buy: $499 $395 at Amazon $499 $395 at Best Buy $499 $395 at B&H Photo The Pocket 3, like its name implies, is compact enough to easily slide into a pocket or small bag, yet still manages to take high quality video. The results are often compared to pricier dedicated mirrorless digital cameras, delivered without the fuss of tweaking exposure or heavy post-processing. It’s capable of shooting up to 4K at 120 frames per second, and while it has built-in microphones, you can connect it to DJI’s Mic Mini wireless mics. While there is a DJI Osmo Pocket 4, it isn’t officially for sale in the United States. Read our DJI Osmo Pocket 3 review . Other deals to consider You can save $10 on your preorder of Nintendo Switch Sports Resort for the Switch 2 at Amazon , bringing the price down to just $49.94, effectively letting you grab the physical release for the same price as the digital version. This title brings back all the minigames from the original Wii title, including bowling and tennis, plus a new open-world mode that introduces activities like skateboarding, and ships out on October 22nd, 2026. Read our review. The Glorious GMMK 2 mechanical gaming keyboard is steeply discounted at Best Buy , bringing the price down to $48.99 (originally $119.99). The compact 65 percent layout includes just the primary letters and numbers, plus arrow keys and few spares for the delete, page up, page down, and end keys. The kit includes Glorious Fox linear switches, but with hot-swappable sockets, you can easily change them out to suit your preference. Keep your Qi-ready devices topped up with a discounted two-pack of Anker Zolo MagSafe-compatible wireless chargers at Amazon for $25.99 (usually $39.99). These chargers have five foot cables with USB-C ports, so you’ll need to supply the wall charger , and support up to 15W of charging power on Qi2-compatible devices.

item.title: New Paris curfew ordered in parts of city from 2100 GMT Tuesday

The fresh curfew runs from 2100 GMT Tuesday to 0400 GMT Wednesday and applies to the Republique public square in the city's central east, where many weekend clashes took place, and in the central les Halles district which is full of shops. FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago reports from central Paris.

I sincerely thank the university, its council, and Senate, and everyone who considered me worthy of this distinction,” she said in a video message days after getting the recognition. “I feel particularly honoured to receive this recognition on Buckingham Africa Day, which celebrates the university’s long-standing relationship with Africa. Africa means a great deal to me; it is a continent of immense potential, creativity, and resilience. I believe deeply in the importance of education, hard work, and creating opportunities for the next generation.” Watch the video below: ﻿ The post VIDEO: Folorunso Alakija Delighted With Buckingham University Honorary Doctorate Award appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Ukraine’s drone rescue of wounded soldier puts much touted idea into practice
item.description: Ukraine’s unprecedented drone rescue of a wounded soldier from the battlefield has shown once again how battlefield necessity can spur innovation. The operation was revealed just days after separate Ukrainian drones designed for casualty evacuation were deployed for frontline testing—taking a step beyond the US military’s decades of experimentation with similar concepts. The drone evacuation of the injured soldier took place at an undisclosed time and place on the frontline where the presence of Russian drones and landmines made it impractical to send in a wheeled ground robot , according to The Kyiv Independent . On October 19, Ukraine’s Army shared a video of the drone evacuation, showing the wounded soldier securing himself in a harness suspended beneath a heavy hexacopter drone with six rotors before being flown to safety. “This is a historic event, the next stage of evacuating the wounded, which we will all come to,” said Napalm, a programmer of the 92nd separate assault brigade's unmanned ground systems company, who went by his callsign per Ukrainian military practice, in a statement. “Now the serious systematic work begins, so that such missions are carried out constantly.” Read full article Comments

item.title: Quantum error correction goes well beyond breakeven
item.description: Running complicated algorithms on quantum computing hardware is going to require the use of logical qubits, where collections of hardware qubits are linked together in ways that allow errors to be detected and corrected. In general, the more hardware qubits you dedicate to each logical qubit, the better the chances are of identifying errors. But, given that the hardware qubits are prone to errors, adding more of them also increases the probability that errors will occur. If the hardware error rate is too high, then growing the logical qubit will only make matters worse. Fortunately, several companies have demonstrated hardware where the error rate is not too high. Several demonstrations show logical qubits are beyond the breakeven point, where adding more qubits improves performance. The problem is that the improvement isn't very dramatic. To lower error rates to levels we'll need to run complex algorithms, we'd have to add a completely impractical number of qubits to each logical qubit. On Monday, Quantinuum announced that its current generation of hardware is capable of scaling well beyond the breakeven point. Each step up in the size of logical qubits improved some measures of their performance by a factor of over 10. Read full article Comments
item.dc:creator: John Timmer
item.content:encoded: Running complicated algorithms on quantum computing hardware is going to require the use of logical qubits, where collections of hardware qubits are linked together in ways that allow errors to be detected and corrected. In general, the more hardware qubits you dedicate to each logical qubit, the better the chances are of identifying errors. But, given that the hardware qubits are prone to errors, adding more of them also increases the probability that errors will occur. If the hardware error rate is too high, then growing the logical qubit will only make matters worse. Fortunately, several companies have demonstrated hardware where the error rate is not too high. Several demonstrations show logical qubits are beyond the breakeven point, where adding more qubits improves performance. The problem is that the improvement isn't very dramatic. To lower error rates to levels we'll need to run complex algorithms, we'd have to add a completely impractical number of qubits to each logical qubit. On Monday, Quantinuum announced that its current generation of hardware is capable of scaling well beyond the breakeven point. Each step up in the size of logical qubits improved some measures of their performance by a factor of over 10. Read full article Comments

item.title: Magic: The Gathering Star Trek Shakes Up Commander With 2 Bold New Mechanics
item.description: Wizards of the Coast began releasing preconstructed Commander decks each year starting in 2011, but ended the Commander series in 2019. New decks have instead rolled out alongside some of its major Magic: The Gathering set releases. While these decks have provided plenty of powerful cards, they haven’t changed with the format with new keyworded mechanics like Lieutenant , which was added in Commander 2014, or Eminence , which debuted in Commander 2017. That’s changing in November, when the Star Trek Universes Beyond set will add two new Commander-specific mechanics.

item.title: Magic: The Gathering Star Trek Officially Adds a New Way to Lose the Game
item.description: The vast majority of Magic: The Gathering games end when one player is reduced to zero life, though some players love to build decks around the more unusual ways to achieve victory. You can empty your opponent’s deck, infect them with poison counters, or try to fulfill the win conditions of cards like Simic Ascendancy or Doctor Doom, Unrivaled . Next month, the Star Trek Universes Beyond set will introduce a whole new way to lose based on one of James T. Kirk’s most famous stories.

item.title: Jeff Bezos is playing the long game with Blue Origin (op-ed)
item.description:
Daniel Biedermann is a Partner at NewSpace Capital, a private equity firm investing in high-growth space companies. He has more than 30 years' experience in the space industry and was previously SVP of Corporate Strategy at SES, where he played a leading role in acquisitions and the creation of joint ventures, including LuxGovSat. Before joining SES, he held engineering and mission management roles at Arianespace and Contraves Space, working on more than 40 space and launch missions.

Daniel Biedermann is a partner at NewSpace Capital. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . Jeff Bezos , the founder and former CEO of Amazon, recently said that Blue Origin , his space technology company, is likely to go public in the coming years. The announcement has (unsurprisingly) attracted considerable attention, not least because Bezos has spent more than two decades financing the company largely from his personal wealth. He has invested billions of dollars in developing rockets , spacecraft and other forms of technology, often with very little prospect of an immediate return. But although Bezos has now raised the possibility of an initial public offering, he has given no firm indication of when one might happen. He may be right to keep his options open. Bezos founded Blue Origin in 2000. Because he has financed so much of its development by himself , the company has been able to pursue ambitious engineering projects without the financial pressures that publicly listed businesses typically face. But developing reusable rockets, manufacturing spacecraft and building the infrastructure needed for future lunar missions requires extraordinary amounts of capital: These projects can take decades to complete, and even the wealthiest investors must think hard about how best to finance them over the long term. Bezos, then, has good reasons to seek additional sources of investment — particularly as Blue Origin prepares to expand its commercial operations. An IPO would give Blue Origin the means to raise substantial capital from public investors and reduce its dependence on Bezos's personal wealth. The company could then use that money to expand manufacturing, develop new technology and compete for a greater share of the growing space market. Public ownership would also give existing investors the power to sell some of their holdings and could make it easier for Blue Origin to finance acquisitions. But the company would also have to meet the expectations of shareholders, who would expect to see regular evidence of commercial progress. item.dc:creator: Daniel Biedermann
item.content:encoded:
Daniel Biedermann is a Partner at NewSpace Capital, a private equity firm investing in high-growth space companies. He has more than 30 years' experience in the space industry and was previously SVP of Corporate Strategy at SES, where he played a leading role in acquisitions and the creation of joint ventures, including LuxGovSat. Before joining SES, he held engineering and mission management roles at Arianespace and Contraves Space, working on more than 40 space and launch missions.

Daniel Biedermann is a partner at NewSpace Capital. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . Jeff Bezos , the founder and former CEO of Amazon, recently said that Blue Origin , his space technology company, is likely to go public in the coming years. The announcement has (unsurprisingly) attracted considerable attention, not least because Bezos has spent more than two decades financing the company largely from his personal wealth. He has invested billions of dollars in developing rockets , spacecraft and other forms of technology, often with very little prospect of an immediate return. But although Bezos has now raised the possibility of an initial public offering, he has given no firm indication of when one might happen. He may be right to keep his options open. Bezos founded Blue Origin in 2000. Because he has financed so much of its development by himself , the company has been able to pursue ambitious engineering projects without the financial pressures that publicly listed businesses typically face. But developing reusable rockets, manufacturing spacecraft and building the infrastructure needed for future lunar missions requires extraordinary amounts of capital: These projects can take decades to complete, and even the wealthiest investors must think hard about how best to finance them over the long term. Bezos, then, has good reasons to seek additional sources of investment — particularly as Blue Origin prepares to expand its commercial operations. An IPO would give Blue Origin the means to raise substantial capital from public investors and reduce its dependence on Bezos's personal wealth. The company could then use that money to expand manufacturing, develop new technology and compete for a greater share of the growing space market. Public ownership would also give existing investors the power to sell some of their holdings and could make it easier for Blue Origin to finance acquisitions. But the company would also have to meet the expectations of shareholders, who would expect to see regular evidence of commercial progress. This, I suspect, is why Bezos wants to establish a stronger business before committing to a listing. It might have much to prove commercially, but Blue Origin’s technical progress has been remarkable. In January 2025, its New Glenn rocket reached orbit for the first time — a significant achievement for a vehicle built to compete in the heavy-lift launch market. The company has also secured government and commercial contracts and continued developing its lunar capabilities. But it will eventually have to demonstrate that it can launch New Glenn frequently, reliably and at a commercially competitive cost, and it is still some way away from that point. Some will be asking whether Bezos wants to raise money to accelerate growth or simply to reduce the amount he himself must invest. Such doubts could affect the company's valuation and make it harder to attract investors who share its long-term ambitions. But again, this suggests Bezos is playing the long game. And given the enthusiasm that has surrounded some billionaire-led space ventures, this is sensible. Investors have sometimes attached extraordinary valuations to companies with ambitious plans but limited commercial experience. Space businesses certainly require ambition: engineers will often spend years developing technology before they can sell it. But investors have to distinguish between technical achievement and commercial performance. At the end of the day, they are seeking a strong rate of return. Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket launches NASA's ESCAPADE Mars mission on Nov. 13, 2025. (Image credit: Blue Origin) What’s also worth considering is how Blue Origin's progress could benefit the wider space industry, particularly the specialist companies that supply technology to larger manufacturers and operators. SpaceX has achieved remarkable success in part by developing and manufacturing much of its technology internally. This includes its rockets, spacecraft and satellites . Blue Origin also does something similar, undertaking substantial engineering and manufacturing work itself, but it is not quite so vertically integrated, and thus may have greater scope to work with external suppliers as it expands. It already buys parts, equipment and services from hundreds of businesses. If it can successfully increase its production and launch activity, these suppliers could receive more orders and gain opportunities to develop new technologies. That’s to the good of the sector as a whole. Why? Because a successful space industry needs more than a handful of large launch providers. It needs companies specializing in satellite communications, propulsion, electronics, software and other areas. Such businesses may have developed highly sophisticated products, but they need bigger customers and predictable demand to expand and produce more. Blue Origin could become an important customer for some of these, particularly if it chooses to buy specialist technology rather than make everything internally. Greater competition between the bigger space companies could translate to more potential customers for suppliers and fewer dependent commercial relationships. Investors would benefit. There’s real potential in businesses that provide the technology and services on which larger space companies depend — the ‘picks and shovels.’ These can sometimes serve several customers and markets, making them less dependent on the success of a single program. A growing Blue Origin would create more opportunities for companies like these — although, of course, much will depend on how Bezos chooses to organize its supply chain. We shouldn’t assume that Blue Origin will become more open to external suppliers than its competitors, but the possibility is at least worth entertaining. As it is, Bezos still faces substantial challenges. Blue Origin is not yet a commercially mature business. The company must increase its launch activity; it must demonstrate its reliability; and it must compete for customers in the public and private sectors. It must also decide how much technology to manufacture internally and whether and where third parties can provide better products or products at a lower cost. Bezos has the resources to give the company time to answer these questions, and he appears to be willing to use them. If he continues to prioritize commercial performance before pursuing an IPO, then Blue Origin could eventually enter the public markets in a much stronger position.

item.title: Folorunso Alakija Receives Honorary Doctorate From UK’s University of Buckingham
item.description: Folorunso Alakija with Vice-Chancellor Professor David Cole at the University of Buckingham. From fashion and banking to oil and gas, Nigerian businesswoman and philanthropist Folorunso Alakija has built a career across several industries. Now, the University of Buckingham in the United Kingdom has recognised her achievements with an honorary doctorate, celebrating her contributions to business, philanthropy and society. The honour was conferred on Friday, 16 October 2026, at the university’s Radcliffe Centre during Buckingham Africa Day, as the institution marked its 50th anniversary. Dressed in a red doctoral gown, Alakija received the degree from Vice-Chancellor Professor David Cole , with family, friends and members of the university community in attendance. For Alakija, the occasion was also an opportunity to speak to the next generation about ambition, responsibility and the importance of creating opportunities for others. Folorunso Alakija in her doctoral gown at the University of Buckingham conferment ceremony. Accepting the honorary degree, she thanked God and the university for the recognition, sharing her belief in Africa’s potential and the responsibility that comes with achievement. “Africa is a continent of immense potential, creativity and resilience and that achievement carries responsibility to serve others,” she said. She also encouraged students and young people to pursue their goals with passion, perseverance and diligence, while remaining humble and recognising the value of their contributions. Her message reflects a career that has taken her through several fields. Before becoming widely known for her work in oil and gas through Famfa Oil, Alakija worked in banking and established herself in Nigeria’s fashion industry. She has also been involved in real estate, printing and philanthropic initiatives supporting education, women and vulnerable communities. Folorunso Alakija with Dean of Faculty Professor Debarpita Bardhan-Correia at the Radcliffe Centre. During the ceremony, Professor Debarpita Bardhan – Correia , Dean of the Faculty of Business, Humanities and Social Sciences, spoke about Alakija’s commitment to opening doors for others. Professor Shalom Lloyd MBE also highlighted the importance of investing in young Africans, asking, “What better investment can we make than developing Africa’s future leaders?” After the conferment, Alakija spent time with students and guests at a reception hosted in her honour, offering advice and encouragement. Her son, Dele Alakija , and sister, Arinola Ogbara , were among the family members who joined her for the celebration, alongside friends and other guests who travelled from Nigeria. The honorary doctorate adds another chapter to Alakija’s journey, one that began long before her success in the oil industry. And as she celebrated the recognition in Buckingham, her message to young people was clear: pursue your ambitions, remain committed to your work and use what you achieve to create
